Sentence: I have the more expensive Shuttle Art brush tip markers which I love, but find it hard to draw a very fine line with them (they are described as 1-5mm brush tip markers).

These no frill ones work just fine.

Sentence: I did notice sometimes the pens would appear to dry out as others noted in reviews, but with a few shakes or some pressure on the tip, I've been able to get the pens to start working perfectly again in no time.
Content: I used these acrylic pens to paint rocks. It was my first time painting rocks so I was unsure what products to buy. I first used acrylic paint and brushes for the background on my rocks. After they dried, I used these pens for the details and all the writing. Overall they were great. I can have a shaky hand and inconsistent handwriting on paper but I think most of the handwriting came out pretty good on the rocks. Every once in awhile, if the rocks had a little dip or crack or something in it, the marker would catch and mess up my writing. I'd just paint over it and wait for it to dry then try again. Luckily this didn't happen very often. Think that's more of a rock painting issue though, not a problem with the product. When writing, I learned to write very slowly. If you go to fast the tip will sling paint. If you go slow, you'll have a much better result. I did notice sometimes the pens would appear to dry out as others noted in reviews, but with a few shakes or some pressure on the tip, I've been able to get the pens to start working perfectly again in no time. I've painted over 100 rocks (some a few times - when i didn't like something about my first try 😅) and all of the pens are still fully functioning and seem to have plenty of paint left. The white pen, which is one of the ones I've used the most, has started to crack a little on the tip (see picture). I think it may just be because I'm writing on uneven rocks though. If I don't pay attention, the cracked tip makes the handwriting very bad as it causes the paint to come out inconsistently. I just make sure to tilt the white pen a certain angle and it works just as it did when I first bought it. I do wish the pens differentiated between the finer and medium point tips. I threw them all in one box and the pens have no markings to indicate if they're fine point or not. Luckily, both tips seem to work fine for what I'm using them for. There's not a huge difference between the two but it would be nice to know. Overall, great pens. Definitely recommend!

Sentence: They dry quickly, but that's acrylic for you.
Content: For anyone that started out drawing and finds the switch to painting to be outside their comfort zone, these are excellent. Even trying them out for writing, I really liked the way they handled, and let me put a tiny bit of flourish into my handwriting. But for painting, I also found that these are great for applying a bit of color and then mixing on canvas, which is advice I heard in a painting class but didn't click until years later. They dry quickly, but that's acrylic for you. They also do live up to the waterproof claim once they're fully dry. These made me go back to an old painting, in fact I haven't painted at all in a long while, and it felt so quick and easy to get into it, rather than preparing a palette and everything. I'd suggest shaking and prepping a number of pens so you can quickly grab colors and draw them in, then take a damp brush and blend them once they're on the canvas. It was so much closer to the digital painting skills I've been developing, and was a lot of fun.

Sentence: If you're going to buy them search Amazon and buy the least expensive - you'll know they're the same because of the box design and the lettering on the pens.
Content: I call these "generic Chinese pens" because the box and pens don't have a company/brand name on them, and I've seen the same set for sale on Amazon under at least 2 different company names. If you're going to buy them search Amazon and buy the least expensive - you'll know they're the same because of the box design and the lettering on the pens.  The quality is pretty average for this type of pen.The instructions on the included 'instruction manual' say to shake them at least 30 times before using and I found out why - if you don't mix them thoroughly before each use you can end up with watery thin paint, or tiny clumps of paint. The description calls them 'extra-fine' - I'd  call it medium fine but they do make good lines.  In my opinion the color selection is just OK - I'd like to have a brighter green and blue than these. I did a swatch chart so you can judge for yourself, but note the colors are not numbered or named on the pens or caps, and the cap color is only a general indication of the paint color.  I couldn't get the colors to blend well either when they were both wet, or by overlaying one color on another dry color.  The colors do show up pretty well on black paper which is a plus to me (see the doodle I uploaded). On the down side these seem to be very wet paints even when thoroughly mixed and they do bleed through thin paper.  I haven't used them on rocks, plastic or ceramics but I suspect they would be better suited for those materials.  If you do use paper you'll probably want to use a heavier weight (like for watercolors or mixed media).  Because of the wetness they take a bit longer to dry than other acrylic pens I've used.Important: You'll need to prime these after mixing before the first use - quickly press the tip straight down on some scrap material and release - you'll see the nib (tip) fill with paint.  I'd recommend using cardboard as there's a good chance of ending up with a puddle or drips.  Also I'd recommend doing a line on scrap paper before actually using to remove any excess paint from the nib.  The instructions say if one gets clogged you can remove the nib and wash it out with warm water, but I'm not going to try that as it would undoubtedly make a mess.  I have yet to use these where I didn't end up with a little paint on my hand.  As far as storage, the box isn't going to last long - if you do buy these I'd recommend keeping them in a cheap pencil case (there are plenty on Amazon).  All in all these are OK pens for casual use at the current price, but if you want professional quality definitely look elsewhere.

Sentence: The project was decorating ceramic vases with these markers and then filling them with a small bouquet of flowers.
Content: I took a big gamble and purchased these for a Valentine's day project for a 5th grade class of 28 students.  The project was decorating ceramic vases with these markers and then filling them with a small bouquet of flowers.  For this project to work well with so many students there was a lot of pressure on the markers themselves - they needed to work well with minimal frustration, be vibrant, DRY QUICKLY, not leak all over the place, and not bleed with washing at home.  I have to say, these exceeded all my demands and expectations.  I don't often write reviews but WOW these markers are well worth the money.  Further, we decorated several leftover vases at home and have washed them several times with absolutely no color bleed, cracking, or fading.  Honestly the vases look like they were professionally glazed.  These markers are fantastic and I highly recommend!

Sentence: They are highly pigmented colors and not transparent.
Content: These acrylic paint markers really did impress me with their quality and the amount of colors you receive for the price. The value for your money is very good and these are quite nice. I like the range of colors that it contains and the box that it comes in is pretty good for storage too. It opens from the top and has a flat bottom so it stands up and you can easily swap markers out without having to close it up and open it up each time while you are in the middle of a project. These paint pens also are super quick to get started and flowing in comparison to other brands that I have tried. These take maybe 2-4 seconds to start up and get the color going when you use it for the first time which is so fast and not a hassle at all. As for the flow and saturation of the markers, I am very pleased. They are highly pigmented colors and not transparent. They make nice solid color that dries rather fast so you can easily layer another color over the top without worrying about smudges. It also seems line you don’t have to really do a ton of coats to get a nice solid streak free color, but I haven’t tried it on a ton of different materials yet so this is still up for review. I also really like the size of the nib that these come with. I am not a fan of paint pens with a very fine tip as they tend to get clogged up quickly snd I just don’t think that I usually want a fine tip when I am looking to use a paint pen. I am usually looking to cover a larger area or a material that is not traditional paper so a broader tip is usually the way I achieve what I am wanting with a paint pen and these markers are the perfect size. Overall, I think these are super awesome quality for the price and I may switch to these for my main paint markers from a more expensive brand that are my go to. These are just as good, if not better in some aspects. These are great for any level of artist from beginner to professional, and I think this set would be great for gifting as well.

Sentence: They seem to pump/fill a bit faster than Poscas, although they are extremely similar at a much more reasonable price point.
Content:
Very much like Poscas. Some of the colors look identical, in fact, including one of the yellows, the light green, the red, and the black and white. The blues and purples are different. They seem to pump/fill a bit faster than Poscas, although they are extremely similar at a much more reasonable price point. The yellows seemed a bit more opaque. Same factory maybe?? Required little shaking to get them started compared to other markers I've used. Love them. Wish they had more colors and other sizes/nibs.

UPDATE: I bought the new 36 set and the paint seemed a bit thinner. There is a nice range of blues and purples, although they could've varied the tones (or even the hues) of the purples. Same for the yellows. When overlapping to fill a larger area, the sheen is a bit different ranging from matte to satin.

I need to compare these to the first set I got. Several colors are like Poscas, but they have unique colors not available in the Posca line, including the yellows and the cool greens. One criticism of this set is that except for the really light green, they are all blue-leaning greens. This set needs one or two warm greens. An emerald or middle-of-the road green.

It seems like the selection of colors was intentional in the way they filled in the missing Posca colors, but also careless as they should have spent more time tweaking the colors. The oranges have a lot of white in them. Similar to Posca, but too much white. This is just one example of where they needed to put forth more time before releasing a product.

Definitely the sheen, film of these markers is different from Posca. Posca's are all matte (you can feel the roughness). It took a lot of chemistry to develop this as every pigment has its own sheen (yes, some pigments are glossy and need added agents to make them more matte).

One of the markers released liquid orange paint that flew through the air when I used it (and landed on my table). These definitely seem more liquid than the other sets I bought. So, nitpicking aside, I like these.

They work well with Poscas and are very similar except not quite as matte or consistently matte. As a standalone set, the greens are lacking in hues. But for the money you pay, they're a nice addition to a marker collection.

The listing now says they are lightfast. I am going to test them, as Posca reds, pinks, browns (and probably purples) fade a lot, and the lightfast ones available from other companies don't perform as well as these or Poscas as Liquitex and Amsterdam have not perfected their paint formulas (they have been selling markers long enough to make them better quality also).

Being lightfast is huge, if, in fact they are, and it would be nice to see this company share how they were tested--or include lightfast ratings. One other marker dealer, Tooli-Art claims to be lightfast, but the proof is in the pudding, and when companies don't rate the lightfastness or the testing standards, it doesn't lend a lot of credibility to the claims, but let's hope this, that SFAIH is telling the truth and their reds, pinks, and purples are really lightfast, which makes them truly artist grade...

After using these, I was able, after letting them dry for a couple weeks, to use a brush-on, Liquitex matte varnish full strength, no fussing. Note, I was able to do this with Poscas too. The key is to let the paint sit for a length of time, not try to do it the same day or even the next day because they will bleed if the paint has not cured. One you use a matte or other varnish, the discrepancies in finish disappear.

One more feature to mention, these have numbers available on the ends for your charts. Will they be sold open stock? Would be lovely to see these in small nib sizes with nib replacements (I am wondering if they will take Posca nibs)... Great Buy.

Sentence:
I had never heard of such a thing before ordering this set.

The markers are simple to use.
Content:
These markers are great FUN! And, yes, they actually deliver OPAQUE ACRYLIC PAINT. I had never heard of such a thing before ordering this set.

The markers are simple to use. You press down to start the paint flowing, and the more you press the marker down or the longer you press, the more paint flows down the nib. Hence you can make somewhat wider or thinner lines, even though the range is limited. The lines themselves are uniform, and the flow is consistent.

The paints adhere very well, as you would expect from acrylic paint. They dried quickly and the colors remained beautifully vibrant (see pic).

The paints are quite opaque on white, but might need a second coat on a dark substrate. (see pic)

I've found them perfect for outlining large shapes, and mistakes can be cleaned up with a q-tip and water before they dry.

They are useful for rock painting and can be used for 'dotting', the dots from them are beautifully round. You can also paint on glass, plastic, wood, etc. with them.

One last thing I'd like to mention: I would love to see these markers with a range of different sizes of nibs, if that's possible. I had to use a fine sharpie, not the acrylic markers, for the fine purple lines in the hair on my picture.

CONCLUSION: For the current price of $18.99, I believe these pens are a really great value. I've had a blast using them.

Content:
I purchased these paint pens for my wife. She uses them for her rock painting hobby.

The pens are well-made but a little smaller than other brands we have used. They prime very quickly and paint smoothly with no blobs or leaks.

The paint used by the manufacturer must have a lot of solids as it covers very well. Even the Yellow pen covers the black outlines with no difficulties. We were really surprised by the quality of the marker pens.

In terms of negatives the only thing we can comment on now is the size of the points which are 2-3mm in diameter. This is a medium sized point that is really good for filling and broad coverage. For work on 2-3" diameter rocks, we wish these points were a little finer.

These marker pens are well made and meet the descriptions and images shown on the website. The paint pens work very well and provide very good first coat coverage. Content: I bought these for painting presentation and auction pieces only to find that color is inconsistent.I got different shades of the color while using a single color. The color doesn't perfectly match stroke-by-stroke.It appears that the pigments separate in the barrel, so as the paint flows it changes in tone, which makes it extremely difficult to get even color. I have even experienced severe whitening and darkening of the single hue to the point of consideration. I have ended up going several times over certain areas of my painting to get the color to even out or at least blend with itself satisfactorily.I have used many acrylic paint markers and these don't particularly stand out to me as a superior marker, actually I found them to be more satisfying to paint with, but less satisfying in end result because of the pigment separation. Because of the separation of pigments my strokes became bothersome and aggravating, and it actually became difficult to match the colors to themselves when trying to cover larger areas. All of the bad experiences I had with color separation happened while using the brush end of the markers, which allows for more flow.There is a wide array of colors, which is nice. The paints do flow well, they cover ok, sometimes they are opaque and sometimes they are semi-transparent... especially when painting over white or black (particularly black shows through other colors quite well requiring several coats to cover thoroughly.)I did find that the fine tip end is pretty good for lining, and similar to a calligraphy nib, you can adjust your pressure to get thicker/thinner lines.These are ok, for practice maybe, but I wouldn't be depending on these for a go to marker for literal presentation pieces.I can suggest these for kids, for practice, or just general crafting/ coloring use. The color doesn't perfectly match stroke-by-stroke.It appears that the pigments separate in the barrel, so as the paint flows it changes in tone, which makes it extremely difficult to get even color. I have even experienced severe whitening and darkening of the single hue to the point of consideration. I have ended up going several times over certain areas of my painting to get the color to even out or at least blend with itself satisfactorily.I have used many acrylic paint markers and these don't particularly stand out to me as a superior marker, actually I found them to be more satisfying to paint with, but less satisfying in end result because of the pigment separation. Because of the separation of pigments my strokes became bothersome and aggravating, and it actually became difficult to match the colors to themselves when trying to cover larger areas. All of the bad experiences I had with color separation happened while using the brush end of the markers, which allows for more flow.There is a wide array of colors, which is nice. The paints do flow well, they cover ok, sometimes they are opaque and sometimes they are semi-transparent... especially when painting over white or black (particularly black shows through other colors quite well requiring several coats to cover thoroughly.)I did find that the fine tip end is pretty good for lining, and similar to a calligraphy nib, you can adjust your pressure to get thicker/thinner lines.These are ok, for practice maybe, but I wouldn't be depending on these for a go to marker for literal presentation pieces.I can suggest these for kids, for practice, or just general crafting/ coloring use. I would not suggest them for presentation artwork, fine application, or any application where consistency and quality are a key factor.I gave the item three stars because of the disappointing color separation.I do suggest this item with heed to application needs.

Sentence: For instance I used one to write on the lid of a jar of pigment to label it, no smudging once it was dry which was excellent.Mostly I tested these on mixed media paper, some of the fine point sides were a little dried out and required wiping off before they would work.
Content: I have no experience with acrylic markers. Acrylic paint yes and markers of various types yes, but not this style, but I wanted to try them out since I collect various art supplies. I hoped they would behave like overly large gel pens and give me the ability to add some details over black ink or black paint, and they do that, but there is more going on. For instance I used one to write on the lid of a jar of pigment to label it, no smudging once it was dry which was excellent.Mostly I tested these on mixed media paper, some of the fine point sides were a little dried out and required wiping off before they would work. It was a learning experience, my silly illustration turned out a lot more pop art since you layer rather than shade in a gradient to get dimension (in contrast with the alcohol markers which can give you a softer edge, these want a much more harsh distinct lines) these are really not the style I usually work with, but since they are waterproof (I did an ink wash over the whole piece once dried) I could do some really fun mixed media pieces with ink and paint. There is little to no smell and they dry fairly quickly, since they can go on multiple surfaces I find myself wondering if I can add an interesting mural to the side of my boring black computer desk. I am glad I got these markers and look forward to integrating them more in my art and seeing what other weird things I can do with them.

Sentence: They are easy to use on every surface I've tried, whether ceramic, stones, fabric or paper.
Content: These acrylic paint pens come in a strong card storage box. It is recommended to keep the box horizontal to encourage even distribution of the paint within the pens. Also, of course, one keeps the pens capped.The pens are slim and comfortable in the hand. Each pen is double-ended, offering a 'brush' width and a pointed end. The color range is phenomenal and includes fifteen metallics. The choice of blues and greens is excellent, whilst the yellows are not quite so well served. The sixty pens in the range offer both tints and shades with some very subtle tones. It's exciting to open the box and see them all waiting to be used.Opacity varies with the colour. I usually shake pens before use but obviously it's better to store them in the horizontal as recommended. I don't know the life span of the pens because I tend not to use things to destruction. I think the price is good  for such a range, especially with the choice of brush/pen tip. They are easy to use on every surface I've tried, whether ceramic, stones, fabric or paper. Certainly they are far less mess than a traditional brush and water pot and consequently can be used in a smaller work space. I'm really pleased with them.

Sentence: The colors flow smoothly from marker to page.
Content: I'm a multimedia artist for both the eyes and the ears, and I've been looking for my voice while making my own album covers. I figured some good-quality paint markers would be a great way to get started, and gosh am I glad I started with these.The colors received are all unique, and they're various levels of boldness or subtlety – some of them are even shimmery! The colors flow smoothly from marker to page. The fine tip is a bit stiffer than I'm used to, but the brush tip is a borderline-luxurious experience. It was quick and easy to fill out a fun little sketch-page. The paint dries fast – not quite enough time to do a proper smudge after a stroke, if that's the style I wanted – but honestly that works perfectly for the type of art I like to make. Also, the caps nestle nicely into each other, so you can pop it on the opposite end as you draw – but they're not very tight, so do still be careful with that.So would I recommend 'em? Long story short, yeah! These are great! (Especially if you're starting out and don't care about brand-name recognition!)P.S. The markers come completely unorganized – not even inserted in the box in a uniform orientation – and if you're anything like me, that's a big relief. It means I can scatter these markers to my heart's content without fretting about returning them just like I found them.

Sentence: The colors are really pretty and the laydown is smooth and not blotchy or clumpy.
Content: I like these Shuttle Art acrylic paint markers. I love that they are dual tipped with a brush end and a fine line tip. The colors are really pretty and the laydown is smooth and not blotchy or clumpy. The lightest colors are somewhat sheer but as the colors get darker, you get full, opaque coverage. The markers are easy to hold and I think the range of colors is fairly well balanced. I'm happy about the brush nib since I plan to use these to color backgrounds on some of my coloring book pages. My only complaint is that they come in a simple cardboard box with no trays and no real way to keep them organized by color family. Will have to get a case for them, but that certainly doesn't take away from my satisfaction with the markers themselves. This is a really nice set.

Content: I got these paint pens mostly for labelling purposes (for those times a black Sharpie just won't cut it!), so if you are thinking to use these in a more artistic venture, perhaps this isn't the most appropriate review. However, these pens are pretty much exactly what I was hoping for; once you prime the pen (which does take a fair bit of pressing the nib) the paint goes on smoothly and thickly. It's a nice,  bright white with a kind of matte finish.Depending on the surface, it can take a while to dry; on cardboard it dries almost instantly, but on really smooth plastics it can take a few minutes. It also is pretty easy to scratch off plastic (but plastic is a hard material to paint; you need specialized formulas, so I'm not super bothered by that). It is waterproof, at least in my minimal testing.Anyway, these are a pretty economical set of white paint markers, that do their job pretty well. I'm quite happy with them.

Sentence: The ink dries fairly quickly but not instantly.
Content: These permanent white acrylic paint markers work fairly well. They were easy to get the paint initially flowing by pushing down repeatedly with the tip. The tip is rather wide so these will not work well for fine line writing. While the paint flows rather well once started, I have had to re prime the tips on a few occasions and I've also had to go back over the paint again to get it thick enough on some materials, particularly those that absorb paint easily such as cardboard. The ink dries fairly quickly but not instantly. For most surfaces I've tried, it takes a minute or two for a thick coat to be completely dry. I've also rubbed it with a wet finger after a minute and the paint smeared slightly. Overall, these pens work well for my crafting purposes.

Sentence: There is no odor and the ink comes out fairly quickly.
Content: These are a decent set of paint pens with a large, broad nib that would be great for graffiti in a large sketchbook or some type of artistic work requiring a broad nib paint pen. These can be used on a variety of surfaces and depending on the angle, you hold it out, you can do different types of strokes. (See pics).Really awesome pro that they blend! But you do need to work fast in order to blend because they dry fast. There is no odor and the ink comes out fairly quickly. The paint is bold, thick and vibrant. These are very easy to use and they perform well. The only thing that they don’t do and this might be a pro or con for you is that they don’t drip. Most graffiti pens will give the drip effect and I did not have that with these. Although I was using this on paper, so if I was using them on a glass window surface for example, standing at an upright angle, I think with enough pressure applied, perhaps I could pull off some drips. Because remember you have to press down in order to get the ink to the nib, so I think if you were to press down when using these, you might pull off some drips, but you’re also going to be wasting a good amount of paint too.But I like them

Sentence: These markers are good for large areas of color that adjoin each other, but if you try to work in layers the solvent in the markers will cause the lower layer to mix and smear unless you work very quickly.
Content: These markers are good for large areas of color that adjoin each other, but if you try to work in layers the solvent in the markers will cause the lower layer to mix and smear unless you work very quickly. Which is fine if that’s what you want, for a sort of painterly effect. But then you have to clean the marker tips off on a scrap piece of paper to get the color back to what it’s supposed to be. None of this is really a surprise though, since pretty much every paint marker I’ve ever used does the same thing.The tips really take some getting used to though. In my experience getting a truly thin line is pretty hard, but wider lines (kinda thick and very thick) are easy. The rectangular tip lends itself well to calligraphy.

Sentence: I've found a bit of a learning curve in getting them primed and making sure they don't drip paint or make a big puddle, but when I manage it well I've been pleased with the results.
Content: This is the first time I've used markers like these, so I can't compare to others like them. I've found a bit of a learning curve in getting them primed and making sure they don't drip paint or make a big puddle, but when I manage it well I've been pleased with the results. I have only used them so far on card stock, glossy and matte, and the colors are bold and appealing. They cover really well so to a certain extent you can layer one on top of another. I'll be continuing to learn and experiment with them, definitely a solid addition to my art supplies.

Sentence: The product is good, dries quickly and will work well for my needs, for the most part.
Content: The product is good, dries quickly and will work well for my needs, for the most part. The description is a bit confusing though. It indicates that you have three width options, from fairly fine to thick (2-3 mm to 15 mm). It also says that the nib is 2-sided. I thought that perhaps the different ends of the nib would have different widths so that it would be fairly easy to get the fine-medium-thick lines but that's not the case. The nib is the same on both ends and you need to play around with the marker to figure out how to get the width you want. The widest is easy, but apparently each side of the nib is cut with slightly different angles so tilting it one way gives you the medium width line and tilting it the other way or rotating the pen will give you the finest line. You can't do real detailed work with this, at least not that I can see. Maybe with a lot of practice. I do think there is a good value to the wider lines but will have to get a fine nibbed pen to do the more detailed work I need this for.

Sentence: I also tested on a smooth plastic bottle, and though it mostly worked you'd want to apply one or more very thin coats to avoid a blotchy, uneven finish.Porous materials like wood, cardboard, fabric, etc.
Content: I ordered these in black to paint the gold metallic frame of a mirror.  The broad, precision felt tips are easier to work with than a brush and the acrylic paint seems to adhere well to the brushed metal finish.  Though the first test coat looked good, I plan on applying a second just for enhanced uniformity and durability.  I also tested on a smooth plastic bottle, and though it mostly worked you'd want to apply one or more very thin coats to avoid a blotchy, uneven finish.Porous materials like wood, cardboard, fabric, etc. should work very well though I can't attest to it being waterproof or UV resistant since I didn't test for that.  During the initial usage you have to firmly depress the felt tip downward for a few seconds for the paint to eventually flow. At first I thought it was defective but was patient and it eventually started working just fine.

Content: These are easy to prime (depress the marker head to get paint flowing after shaking) and have a great flow. Sentence: The problem with most permanent markers (at least for me) is that the ink simply dries out too fast.
Content: I use wide tipped markers when labeling boxes so that I can easily see what's inside from several feet away.  In fact, I use them for labeling just about everything!  The problem with most permanent markers (at least for me) is that the ink simply dries out too fast.  I can't speak to the longevity of the BIGTHUMB markers because I haven't owned them long or used them a lot but if they end up having an even shorter life than the other markers, I will be back to update this review.  For now, I'm going to assume that they have a reasonably long life and I hope that turns out to be the case because I'm delighted with the way they mark.  Because they are paint markers, once the ink is flowing you get great coverage and have the option of making very wide to thin marks with a single stroke. I suppose the life of the marker will also greatly depend upon the size stroke you make with it; for my purposes, the medium to smaller tip is perfect.  The one caution I would give is that they do take a bit longer to dry than regular permanent markers because the pens are dispensing acrylic paint rather than ink.  Marks are still relatively quick drying but not instant drying so take a bit of extra care, particularly when the markers are first used, so that you don't smudge your work or end up with paint all over yourself!

Sentence: You do have to press down to get the paint to flow but I really prefer that to having my marker tips dry out and become useless.The case is cute and convenient and the color assortment covers all the essentials.
Content: I have a number of different types of acrylic markers and they all do what they say they intended to do. But there’s something about Uniball/Posca products the consistently put them in a class of their own. These paint markers absolutely live up to the brand promise. It’s just so fun making every day stuff pretty with these markers.

Sentence: ) It also does not have any "holiday" packaging aside the very nice hard side (?) case that the markers come in which I suppose makes it giftable.
Content: I've never used Posca markers before, but having recently entered the adult coloring community, I have heard others sing their praises, and now I can say, rightfully so.  This "holiday" set of 22 markers is really 11 makers of the 3 m and 5 M variety.  Same colors - just different sizes.  The colors include:  black (a beautiful opaque black) and white (equally gorgeous for a paint marker), pink, lavender, light pink, blue, orange, sunshine yellow, light green, aqua green, and sky blue.  I'm not sure why this termed a holiday set.  It is coming out near Christmas and yet the set does not contain what you might consider a traditional Christmas red or green.  (Actually, if you get the larger 62 count set, I bet there is one in it. )  It also does not have any "holiday" packaging aside the very nice hard side (?) case that the markers come in which I suppose makes it giftable.  So there's that.  But the markers themselves are kind of impressive for what they are.  The paint/ink is smooth.  It comes easily off the tip with streaking or skipping.  The color is bright and yet opaque.  I just wrote some words with the colors on marker paper and was extremely surprised by the quality.However, my one "concern" is that the markers themselves feel rather light, which makes me wonder exactly how much paint/ink is in them and how long I can expect them to last before I need to replace them.  Posca markers not cheap.  They are at the highest end of paint makers in the field.  Please see the 62 ct set in this listing if you are unsure of what that means.  I guess I just want to know that I'm getting my money's worth at the price point.  I also think that I would have preferred to have this set with more colors at the same size for the price rather repeating the 11 colors just to have two different sizes.  But overall, this is a quality set.  NOW I GET IT.

Content:
I use markers for a variety of crafts, and have purchased way too many glitter, metallic and other specialty markers online and from local craft stores.

WHAT MAKES THIS A GOOD SET:
First, that you get so many different styles of markers in one big box that's easy to store. Anyone that has priced buying these in small sets or even individually will appreciate that.
The glitter pens are pretty glittery. I have a few glitter pens that are a different brand that are more glittery, but they were expensive pens that I had to buy individually from a local craft store. For the price of these, the glitter effect is pretty good.
The metallic markers are also pretty good. The effect is comparable to other brands I have that cost slightly more than these.
You get a good variety of colors in the Classic, Pastel, Neon, Morandi (which are "muted" colors btw, vs bright neon colors). The white, and other light-colored markers do a great job - bright and easy to see on dark paper.

THINGS TO KEEP IN MIND:
When you want to use one of these markers, you kinda have to "get them flowing" initially. They printed a little diagram on the side showing you how to pump them to get them flowing. If you're not getting a very strong, bold line, you need to pump the marker some more, to get the ink flowing better.
Due to the nature of how ink flows from these markers, you can get the best result using them if you're very purposeful in your marks. If you want to make quick, very fast marks, these may not be the pens for you.

- My biggest complaint is the box they come in. The way that this box is depicted in the product description pictures makes it seem like it arrives in a tiered, organized box. It's just a box. It's a nice box, but it's just a box, without any tiers or dividers. The markers themselves are numbered, and the back of the box has a chart or "key" that you can use, to identify what type of marker each number is.
Additionally, the names of the actual colors are not on the box, nor are they on the markers themselves. This might not bother you, but for colorblind folks like myself, not having the actual name of the color written on these markers can be a bit of an issue.

Overall, this is a good variety of specialty markers that I'm sure to get a lot of use out of.

Sentence: I wish the packaging and came in was more sturdy and not the flimsy plastic.
Content: The only reason why I’m rating these markers three out of five stars is because of the size. They are extremely small and have thin barrels. Also another downside is that if you run out of one color, you would possibly have to rebuy a pack to get the color than buying it individually. Overall they’re good but not great. I’m not head over and heels with love with them.

Sentence: No chunky blotches, no drips, and no smearing.
Content: Instead of having a traditional guestbook at my wedding, I decided to have a sign to put up along with wedding pictures, for our guests to write their messages on.I got a wood sign, in gray. I didn’t want people to write all over it in black sharpie, since this sign will be part of my home decor, I don’t want black sharpie writing displayed on my living room wall. I decided that white writing would look nicest against the gray background.I came across these paint pens. I liked the idea of using permanent acrylic paint instead of ink. I also liked that these were extra fine tip, which would make writing easier.I tested them out as soon as I got them, because I wanted to know if they’d be any good, or if I’d need to get different ones. I had a piece of scrap wood that was close to being the same gray as the sign. The directions said that before using them the first time, to press the tip down a couple of times to get the paint to flow down to the tip of the pen. I did that with both pens a couple times on my scrap wood, until each one left a circle of paint. I tested writing with each pen, and they were super easy to write with. The flow of the paint was nice and steady, and consistent.The wedding was a few weeks later. We were outdoors, in 104 degrees. Both pens continued to work perfectly. No chunky blotches, no drips, and no smearing. I posted a photo of how the sign that was written on with these pens, but the pic honestly doesn’t do it justice. In person, the white paint is a little more vibrant and bright. To put it simply, the white POPS!

Sentence: POSCA markers are wee bit more expensive for a little less in markers.INK: The ink is so OPAQUE!
Content: I’m 🤩OBSESSED🤩!PRICE: It is $20 original price for the 12 pack of markers, but that’s already amazing! POSCA markers are wee bit more expensive for a little less in markers.INK: The ink is so OPAQUE! It’s amazing! On white paper you don’t need to coat what so ever! It’s just one marking and it results in solid color! I didn’t have actual black paper to test, but printing out a black photo worked. So the ink of the marker might be different in usage on regular black colored paper versus printed ink black paper lol. Anywaysss, it did take a few coats for it to pop on the black paper like it is in the picture, but it still did amazing! The ink didn’t dry to a different color.OVERLAPPING: The colors look great and work great overlapping! You might need a few coats for the color white, but they do amazing!CONDITIONS OF PAPER: IT DID NOT BLEED THROUGH!!! That was the most exciting part of it all! The paper does warp a little but that doesn’t bother me none. (Demonstrated on the last picture) I would say it did leave some texture on the paper too like if you took a regular marker like the crayola ones on construction paper and colored the same spot over and over again and the paper starts to peel a bit-yeah that’s what it feels like, but very slightly (keep in mind it still didn’t bleed)PRESSURE/MARKER TIP: the tip of the marker is so soft so no pressure is needed which is actually pretty cool because you don’t need more pressure to get more color payoff.You don’t need to shake them either to get it started with ink. Just take the cap off and you’re ready to color!!!OVERALL: Just such an amazing product! I’m just so shocked that regular markers like crazy art, crayola and off brands included-make streaks and can never be the same color when you’re overlapping with them as they start to bleed through when you’re coloring. (Demonstrated on the page that says “This book belongs to:” on the front and back)Sharpie, if you’re reading this PLEASE make more colors!!!! I’ll buy them right now!!! As a pack though. Because having to buy multiple packs for different colors is a pain and a waste of packaging. But please pretty please! 🥺🫶🏼They are PHENOMENAL 🤌🏽🤌🏽!!

Sentence: These Sharpie water-based acrylic markers are great for writing on just about any surface.
Content: These Sharpie water-based acrylic markers are great for writing on just about any surface. They write smoothly & evenly without blotchy ink deposits. Vibrant, bold colors. Very pigmented & doesn't take multiple attempts to get good solid lines or coverage. Water-based, so no strong odor. Ready to use. You don't have to press, pump or shake to draw the ink into the tip. Wonderful for craft or art projects. Dries quickly to prevent transfer. As a lefty, very much appreciate this! Color indicating caps on top & bottom. Was shocked to see they really don't bleed through paper. In my photo, I just drew a few lines on standard printer paper. Even when writing slowly, no ink bled through. Would love to see more of these with fine tips as well. Overall, incredibly impressed with the quality of these sharpie markers!

Sentence: And the ink dries quickly, which is just another huge advantage when using the art pens on different mediums.
Content: I really enjoy making jewelry. In fact I have been to several jewelry/fossil shows where I buy pieces that I love. Many of the stones are just plain, and have no painted edge to make the stones look great after shaping them into the correct size.I have gold acrylic paint in a bottle that I had been using, but it is a huge setup and tear down after completely the job. I also have to use a paintbrush, which I throw out afterwards. It’s too hard to clean. I didn’t enjoy this portion of jewelry making because of all the extra steps in acrylic painting. Finding these Gold acrylic pens was wonderful. Now instead of getting out all the extra materials for what my acrylic pen will do in seconds.Now I just take out my Gold pen and apply the acrylic paint to the exact spot in about 2 seconds. And I can either use the brush side, for more broader strokes, or a fine point, for painting a sharper edge of a stone. I’ve also found that these paints can be used on clothing, canvas, etc. I am so used to doing one thing with the Gold acrylic that I didn’t realize that I could use them on so many other art forms.I tried the inks on both sides, brush, and point. I just did it on a piece of paper, and I very pleased that the ink flowed out into the paper without having to take any measures, like pressing the tip, to make them work. And the ink dries quickly, which is just another huge advantage when using the art pens on different mediums. I appreciate the manufacturers making the acrylic paint flow easily, dry quickly, stay vibrant, and even the price of the pens is excitable. Besides, how much easier could the manufacturers have made these pens? They are incredibly easy to use.

Sentence: At about $11.00 or 46 cents per marker these double-ended acrylic markers seem to be a really good value for the money.
Content: At about $11.00 or 46 cents per marker these double-ended acrylic markers seem to be a really good value for the money.  I don't have much experience with acrylic markers so I was happy to see that I could try them out for not a whole lot of money, in case I decided that I don't like working with acrylic paint.  I was interested in using them on canvas and they are advertised as being for painting on "multi-surface" - paper, canvas, glass, cermaci and stone.  I like the way the color/paint flows easily and evenly - one or two coats needed at the most.  The colors don't bleed through canvas or "standard/regular" paper which is really nice and actually surprised me.  As far as the colors themselves, the red is really more of a pink than a red but for the most part the colors match what you see on the box.  Most of the colors are opaque  and there are a few metallic colors.  I couldn't really see much of a difference between the two tips - brush vs dot, except when I wanted to paint dots - then it was clear that there is a difference.  But, if not painting "dots" there is really little difference between the two tips.  I tried painting on glass and stone; the paint glided on very easily but took awhile to completely dry - reminded me of how you have to wait for nail polish to dry completely.  Since this is a water based ink I imagine that if you got water on whatever you are painting with these markers, the paint will run and dissolve.  For someone wondering if they would like to paint with acrylic markers, I think this is a nice little starter set for not a whole lot of money.

Sentence: The one thing I haven't done is test how the ink holds up to water/washing.All this to say, I'm really surprised and pleased with what these markers can do and how easy they are to use.
Content: I'm no artist. I'm reviewing these just as a regular non-artist who occasionally needs/wants to do some arty stuff.First I tried these pens on paper. Regular paper. They work great. The colors are good and, surprisingly, nothing bled through, even repeated layers of ink.Next I tried them on fabric. I have some plain canvas bags I use recycling and for my fruit/vegetables at the grocery store. I used the pens to decorate the sides of the bags to make it easy to identify & sort, etc. Again, even with repeated layers of ink and very low thread count/loose weave fabric, there was no color bleeding at all. The one thing I haven't done is test how the ink holds up to water/washing.All this to say, I'm really surprised and pleased with what these markers can do and how easy they are to use. The markers are fun & easy to use and the price is great.

Sentence: 3_ The pens I received all seem to be 'full' with no dried out tips - I tested both ends of each pen.
Content:
Purchased the set of 24 (came in a blue box) - wanted more than just basic colors but didn't want to spend a lot - a good compromise. Haven't used these yet except to test them out, but so far, so good. Pros: 1) they write nice - nice flow, movement, etc. 2) as 'paint' pens, there's no shaking or pressing to get the paint to flow. 3_ The pens I received all seem to be 'full' with no dried out tips - I tested both ends of each pen. 4) The lids all have a nice 'snap' and stay on securely. Cons: 1) The box comes with a swatch on the back, giving each color a name and number - but the pens themselves have neither names or numbers, so you can ONLY go by the lid color. And that's pretty tricky. While testing, I made a mark on the swatch with the best, to me, corresponding colored pen. Some colors are amazingly close, others - not at all. First photo shows how I -mistakenly- marked the 'brown' pen on 'Gingerbread' before realizing it left no swatch for the lighter (tan) color. Yeah - the 'brown' is supposed to be 'Stone Grey' apparently. Go figure. In a case like this, I like to mark the pen on a white label, cut a strip, and stick it around the lid of the pen so I can see the true color. Unfortunately, 2) the lids are all very textured with ridges, so this time I'll have to stick it on the pen itself. But where? not on either end close to the caps (it'd cover the symbol showing which tip is which, & don't want it under my fingers when using the pens) so it'll have to go in the center of pen, annoyingly over the text. Not really any other option.
Overall, I do like the pens and would buy them again - the annoyances are small compared to their quality.
Edit: Added my 'actual color' strip to each pen (except black, white, gold, & silver) and added the color # in case I decide to order a larger variety later. Amazingly, the actual colors are VERY close to the cap colors! Amazing because this isn't usually the case! The photo shows how just 2 of the colors are a bit off - the bright pink & the yellow next to it in the top row. Realized I missed the 'tan' and 'grey' pens after the photo was taken. The tan is spot on, but the grey ... it's the same color as the cap, but lighter. You'd need 2-3 coats to make it the same as the cap.
As for how they work - great! Coverage, even over a dark color, is impressive. On the head shown I used black (for the outlines and the eye area), red, light & dark blue, and white (ONLY for the dots on the black part of the eye). The light blue was over the black of the eye and 2-3 coats gave the color shown.

Sentence: They are made in China, are acid free, &
Content: I want to start this review off with saying that I appreciate the fact that the instructions are on the back of the box for those who aren't sure how to prep this type of marker. They are made in China, are acid free, & water based. There are 12 different colors with silver & gold included. I had no issues with prep or coloring. These markers perform just as good as popular brands especially with the coverage of the versatile rectangle nib. It can create lines ranging 3mm-15mm...fine, med, & jumbo. It's for covering larger areas mostly but the way the nib was designed it comes to a flat point so that you can use it at a tilt to get a slightly smaller line. I've provided such examples in my swatch photo. They dry pretty quickly, quick enough that my hand didn't smear any of the colors/swatch. I also tested the waterproof statement on the blue color on white paper & the color didn't move at all! So that's a true statement. I swatched these on a popular cheaper kids marker/watercolor paper & there was very little bleeding. I think black was the only color that bled through but it was only where there was more than 1 swipe of the marker. I've used these on white boards, rocks, fabric, shells, glass, plastic, & metal. I can't complain about these at all. I'm pleased with them & the fact that my kiddos can use them. I recommend the SRUOLOC markers for students, crafters, hobbies, or in place of your more expensive markers that you want to save for serious works...but these aren't far from the more expensive brands other than the fact that it's only 1 nib which is why I suggest such. I really like them and they're great for learning if nothing else.

Sentence: The markers are advertised as having vibrant colors, but most of them are dull and streaky.
Content: I was really excited to try the SRUOLOC 12 Colors Jumbo Markers for my rock painting and other crafts, but I was let down. The markers are advertised as having vibrant colors, but most of them are dull and streaky. The felt tips are too soft and tend to fray quickly, making it hard to get a clean, smooth line. The paint inside is also inconsistent—it’s either too thick or too watery, and it doesn’t cover well on surfaces like stone or wood. I ended up with smudges and uneven coverage, which ruined my projects. These markers are not worth the price. If you want reliable, high-quality paint markers, look elsewhere.

Sentence: They function about how you'd expect - they're lightweight so easy to hold, they have quite vibrant colors, and they will work on many surface types.
Content:
For the price, these are excellent paint pens. They function about how you'd expect - they're lightweight so easy to hold, they have quite vibrant colors, and they will work on many surface types. I'm using them on a light, unstained wood, and I have to use at least two coats of whatever color I'm using. That being said, the end product is going to look really nice.

The case they come in is not the best, so I would recommend planning for an alternate storage solution. I purchased a separate pen/pencil case for them that will hold them horizontally as is recommended from the product for how to store them.

The fine side writes really fine and nice. The thicker side is all good. If you go in swirls, you can't really see the strokes. That said, I go side to side because I like the look of strokes because it really screams hand painted. You will need to leave whatever project it is to sit and dry. It's still paint, and as such needs to dry. If you grab it right after, you will get paint on yourself. Thus, if you're getting these for children, I would recommend close supervision. Otherwise, I can see people of most ages really enjoying these for art projects, and especially those who may find it difficult to hold certain brushes or those who don't have storage space for lots of brush types, palettes, etc. Paint pens are a nice alternative.

You can paint over your mistakes after they've dried. I have tested that because I don't have the steadiest hand, so I make mistakes often. However, I have not tried to correct a lighter color over a darker color. Only dark over light, so be mindful that it's paint. It will bleed or blend together. Would not recommend for single-use/one-day projects. Most projects with these will need multiple days. I could see this being fun for really unique beading designs if you're making household decor, crafts, jewelry, etc.

Sentence: This is important because on some markers the colors are very different than their caps and when you're making art you want to know what the paint actually looks like.Paint quality: Thin, dries quickly and is very translucent.
Content: I use paint markers to paint rocks.Here's what these are like:Colors: The colors are extremely close, if not exact matches to the marker caps. This is important because on some markers the colors are very different than their caps and when you're making art you want to know what the paint actually looks like.Paint quality: Thin, dries quickly and is very translucent. It takes 5+ coats to cover a surface. One of the biggest problems with these markers is that the colors mix when you layer them. For example, if you paint down green, and then let it dry completely, and then paint white over it it, your white marker will be ruined and pick up the green paint. My other acrylic markers don't do that.Tips: The brush tip is great as a brush. It' makes it easy to do thin lines and also fill in large areas quickly. I do like that you don't have to press the tips to release paint, although sometimes this is frustrating when you want the paint to go on thickly or in more quantity.Overall - Good for kids and teens. Probably best for paper. Not at all appropriate for serious artists.

Content:
First time using paint pens of any kind, so take this review with a grain of salt ofc!!

Was apprehensive about buying something like Posca pens because of the price and not knowing whether or not I’d actually enjoy them, so I decided to try these as like a…trial run I guess.

PROS:

Firstly, they are super easy to use. I particularly like the brush nib because it allows for that line variation and filling in larger areas.
Something to note is that I’m using suuuuuper thin (A5) paper, and so far, after layer upon layer—the paper hasn’t buckled hardly at all!! Was a really nice surprise tbh!! In fact, the only thing that made it buckle and bleed through was the pen I was using for my lines after laying down the paint. I have been having so much fun experimenting with the colors (which there are a lot!!)

CONS:

Be prepared to layer these. They aren’t suuuuper duper pigmented like others I’ve seen especially if you’re laying a light color over a dark one, even after shaking them for a bit as it says to do on the back of the box. (Though in all honesty, I enjoy it more as a feature than a con, but I know some people might not find that appealing—but it could be that I’m impatient and don’t shake them long enough before use)
Something I also noticed is that there are NO lighter/pastel type colors. It’s not a huge deal, but I’d really love a few of those just to lighten things up if I need to. Generally good flow, but some of the markers have little fibers on the nib that need to be picked off. ALSO. Before you start layering, give the first layer a little bit of time to dry. I noticed it takes about 10 seconds but then you’re good to go!!

I will say though, for the price and what you get, they work wonderfully and other than what I listed above I can’t think of any complaints!! Great for anyone like me who hasn’t tried them before and doesn’t wanna break the bank on other brands. :)

No bleeding and the ink is colorfast.  It is just as dark as before the first wash.  I recommend this product for marking/drawing on 100%n cotton fabric.  I also tested it on 100% polyester.  I do not recommend on 100% polyester...the ink bled a lot and the letters were not clear. First photo shows the outlined letters on 100% cotton and the smaller letters printed on 100% polyester.

Sentence: The pens are neatly packaged in a sturdy and organized zipper case.
Content: This set of 80 acrylic paint pens earns a mixed review.  The pens are neatly packaged in a sturdy and organized zipper case.  This makes storing the pens horizontally easy and ensures your art area is not messy.  I laid out the case and took a piece of pre-cut 4X6-inch white cardstock.  I attempted to start drawing with the black pen.  I couldn’t get the cap off the paint pen.  I eventually had to get a rubber gripper that is used to remove jar lids.  I got into a rhythm and was soon able to remove the tops off the sample pens I tried as I drew my drawing.  I needed to twist and pull using the rubber gripping pad.  If you have arthritis, you may have to work around the fact that the tops are incredibly difficult to get off the paint pens.I started with the black pen, creating a basic drawing to fill in with different colors.  First, I used traditional paint markers to fill in the petals of the flowers.  Then, I used several metallic markers to fill in the flower center and leaves.  Finally, I touched up the black ink and attempted to do some detail work.  I colored the four blue corners last.  The three white dots in those corners took three coats with the white acrylic paint marker.  In contrast, the whitish/grey coloring on the stems is one coat with the white marker (see photograph).The paint pens dry fairly quickly.  I got several paint spots on my hands, which I cleaned with a scrub brush, warm water, and hand soap.  The black pen easily covered minimal mistakes made while coloring the petals and center.  I had to use a light touch, or the nib would wear away my paper. I used a metallic pen to color the center of the flowers. The paint flow was too heavy and made a mess when I opened it.  Eventually, that particular marker’s paint flow slowed, and I could continue to use it.I decided to test whether these paint pens are waterproof and quick-drying.  I waited fifteen minutes after I was done with the drawing.  I wetted down a paper towel with three squirts of water and dragged it two times across the right-hand side of the drawing.  The ink did not smear on the paper but lifted off and covered my paper towel (see photograph).  I have concerns about using these paint pens on anything exposed to water.  Paint from both the regular and metallic pens was present on the paper towel.On another 4X6-inch piece of cardstock, I used two colors to write letters, numbers, and common words  (see photograph).  As you can see, the medium-sized nibs make detailed drawing and writing difficult.  The manufacturer does not hide this; few examples of tiny writing or detailing are on the product description page.  Additional acrylic pens to finish your artwork may be necessary, depending on what you are creating.This paint pen set is much better than others I have tried, but it misses the mark with caps that can’t be easily removed and paint that is not waterproof.  Even with that in mind, I believe this is still a good value for 80-paint pens.  This set may work for you if you are a doodler and want to have fun.  However, if you are serious about your art, you may need to look elsewhere to be completely satisfied.

Sentence: Instead of making colorful see through colors, these pens laid down opaque colors.
Content: This set of paint pens I sort of dithered about getting it as I have many markers and wasn't sure if I needed more things in this type of category of art supplies. I am so glad that I got this set of 80 pens which included 24 metallic pens and the rest in regular colors. When I first started swatching the different pens, something I do with any set of colors, I was stunned at what I saw. Instead of making colorful see through colors, these pens laid down opaque colors. They only come with one bullet tip that is fairly narrow.I finished my swatch page and was happy with them and then over this weekend I have had other reasons to use them. I had gotten a package with preprinted canvas boards and little pots of paint like those in a paint by number set, as well as brushes. Even with using the narrowest of brushes, I made a hot mess of the picture and couldn't begin to stay within the lines with the gloppy paint. I tried these paint pens on the board that I had made a mess of and was able to make the leaves and stems much better and then tried coloring in two of the 5 flowers. They did an excellent job! Amazing to see what a better job the pens from this set made. Now I will be able to use them with the rest of the canvases that I got and send the paint pots to the thrift store. I wonder how many times I got discouraged in my art work because the products that I was using weren't up to par, and not knowing that I blamed myself as causing the trouble. I love these paint pens!I apreciate the opportunity to use these pens. Thank you.

Sentence: The manufacturer claims these markers are fast-drying and waterproof.
Content: I drew a small drawing of flowers, testing several paint markers from this kit.  The acrylic paint markers work well on paper.  There is good paint flow without excess paint on the paper.  I had excellent control of paint placement.  Also, the markers did not require any shaking.  The large selection of colors is pleasing.  I let the drawing set for fifteen minutes.  The manufacturer claims these markers are fast-drying and waterproof.  I ran my fingers across the paper’s surface without ink on my fingers.  Next, I wet down a paper towel with a spray bottle.  I rubbed it a few times across the drawing.  (See the result in the photographs.)  These acrylic paint markers are not waterproof.  There is a minor smearing of paint on the paper, and a great deal of paint came off on the paper towel.  This is disappointing and will affect how I can use these markers.  If you plan on using them with any medium exposed to water, you should probably look elsewhere for acrylic paint markers.  I used a lead test swab on the paint in my drawing.  It appears to be lead-free.  I would give these acrylic paint pens more than two stars had the pens been waterproof.  The fact that they are not limits their usefulness.

Sentence: How do you not have black, at the very least, in both sizes?Not only that, it was very streaky on the page.
Content: I should have paid more attention to the details on the description for sure. If you’re planning on using them for crafts - find another brand. I wish I hadn’t wasted my money.

Sentence: They are hard to get started, in that you have to wait a bit to get the pigment to go into the market tip, which is fine, but once it does, it comes out in a glob, and if you are not careful, you get a big paint smear on your painting surface.
Content: I was a bit disappointed by these marker pens.  They are hard to get started, in that you have to wait a bit to get the pigment to go into the market tip, which is fine, but once it does, it comes out in a glob, and if you are not careful, you get a big paint smear on your painting surface.  And the smear does not dry quickly!  I wound up with a lot of messes.  There's a lot of colors included, but most of them are not that vibrant.  They do blend fairly well, and I managed to paint some rocks which, in the cases where I didn't get any big splotches of paint, dried well and look pretty nice, but I've tried other paint markers I liked a lot better.

Sentence: The individual marker caps click to indicate they are closed in a very satisfying way, feeling secure but not overly difficult to open.
Content: Unfortunately, my particular box of markers contained two of T329 and missing T333, which I didn't notice until I was in the process of testing them and transferring to a new holder. I was only given the option to request a return and replacement and ultimately decided against it since I had already started using them. I have my concerns about the delicacy and endurance of the marker nibs. I probably will not use them on anything rougher than cardstock and I'm not sure they would hold up against use on wood or stone unless they are extremely smooth or polished surfaces, but I will admit that I did not attempt this.With that being said, these have to be the best quality acrylic markers I have yet to use. They went on my cardstock paper consistently, smoothly and the colors are still vibrant after drying with no clumping, bumps or bubbles. The paint seems to take other mediums layered over the top well, such as outlining markers. The individual marker caps click to indicate they are closed in a very satisfying way, feeling secure but not overly difficult to open. While not a functional part of the markers, I also really enjoy the clear section where you can see the paint inside.While I am a little disappointed by the missing color from my order, I still would consider purchasing these markers again.

Sentence: All the colors have good to excellent coverage.
Content: I have tried about half a dozen brands of acrylic brush markers and these are among the very best.  I like the selection of colors (I got the set of 36) and have tried them all.  All the colors have good to excellent coverage.  I painted small squares of each color with only one coast of paint on both white and black papers and have attached a picture to this review.  As you can see, the colors with only once rapid coat covers completely (the white spots in some of the colors are only because I missed; I did not want to go back and fill in those spots because then I would create a second coat in some areas).  The coverage for black is very good considering how thin the acrylic ink is for one coat.  If you go over the paint a second time the colors are as vibrant as the ones painted on white paper.  I do wish there were names on the colors, but I guess names are just names and the best way to determine which color you want is to base your selection on the paint brush itself.  The covers on the pens are very close to the actual color but not quite exact; I recommend looking at the nib.  I will be using these pens often.

Sentence: The pens seem well designed in their physical aspects such as the dual tips, flow of paint and secure caps.
Content: The pens seem well designed in their physical aspects such as the dual tips, flow of paint and secure caps. The reason I did not give more stars is the colors. In many cases, the color dispensed from brush tip does not match color from the fine point. Kind of a deal breaker for me. Also, the variety of colors is narrow for the number of pens with several of the pens having colors so similar to others, they are practically the same. This leaves colors out that would have been very nice to have such as a deep viridian, sap green, burnt and raw sienna, burnt and raw umber and deep vibrant reds. So, I will keep looking for a set with good variety and consistency of color. These can go to the kids to play with.

Sentence: I’m really impressed overall with the amount of colors you get for the low price.
Content: This is my first experience using / buying acrylic markers like these. I’m really impressed overall with the amount of colors you get for the low price. Normal professional markers are more than triple the price for a third of the amount. The darker colors are more opaque and some of the colors were already a bit dried out. But that’s not a deal breaker for me. I like the dual tip as well. This set also comes with twelve iridescent markers that are very opaque. The gold is literally liquid gold. I did my first drawing of this turtle and I’m really happy overall. They are easy to layer overtop of each other so if you make a mistake it’s easy to fix and they’re vibrant.I like that the kit comes with extra felt tips and number stickers so the box can stay organized. I did do four stars just because some of the colors were already not usable straight out of the box.

Sentence: I heard about these on TikTok, they were cheaper than the other paint markers I had seen.
Content: I heard about these on TikTok, they were cheaper than the other paint markers I had seen. What drew me into to these were the dual tips. It comes with a fine tip and with brush tip. However, I have found that the nibs fray a bit, and I think I gotta try to figure out how to clean or replace the nib of the white marker I got because the nib isn’t producing the paint. The white marker seemed to dry up less than a month of having them, and I didn’t use them except to swatch. With that being said, all the other markers have been consistent without drying out or having to replace the nibs. They do work and get the job done, I also like that the packaging was nice, the box they came in looks feels sturdy, I haven’t had any problems with it, and it has a magnetic flap. The plastic trays inside are extremely flimsy and are starting to crack on mine but I’m just extra careful. I got these because I wanted more colors- and you do get a lot of color variety. I kept these depict the problems listed- because of the variety of colors and the fine tip nib. It’s come in handy.

Sentence: So many colors!
Content: I LOVE THESE MARKERS! A great value for the quality and price. So many colors! I have been inspired to start drawing/painting again. Experimenting with different blending techniques. I just wish the markers were already numbered because the little stickers fall off very easily. I ended up marking the numbers with the white pen. Worked somewhat but starting to wear off of some of them because I can’t stop using them.

Sentence: Honestly, these markers were really nice and easy to use.
Content: Honestly, these markers were really nice and easy to use. None of the markers were dried out when I got them. I got these as a gift, and they are amazing. What I really like about these markers is that if you make a mistake on your artwork, you can very easily fix it. The only downside about this product is that the white marker doesn't show up well on other colors, because of that I need to use my white Posca marker. I really recommend getting these if you like arts and crafts. I'm normally used to drawing in black and white, but after a bit of messing around with the colors I got everything to work well. Even if you're a beginner artist, these markers can work amazingly in your art pieces. The artwork in my review belongs to me, and as you can tell..the markers show up well.

Sentence: The paint goes exactly where you want it to go with no bleeding.
Content: Bought these as an additional resource to paint my resin printed 3D figures. These markers work great. The colors are very vibrant, especially the metallic ones. The drying time is similar to regualr acrylic paints from Citadel and Vallejo. The paint goes exactly where you want it to go with no bleeding. The fine tip points make it easy on small details like eyes, jewelry and other sometimes hard to reach areas.

Sentence: One of my pens was cracked and therefore dried out, so I notified them, as instructed on the info card.
Content: I love these acrylic markers! The colors are beautiful!  And the customer service is amazing! They include a card with some hints to follow and also some extra tips in case one dries out. One of my pens was cracked and therefore dried out, so I notified them, as instructed on the info card. They immediately sent me a replacement…not just one pen, but a small set that included the one color I needed! Highly recommend!

Sentence: While it’s great to have so many colors, I wish they were more opaque, especially the lighter colors.
Content: While it’s great to have so many colors, I wish they were more opaque, especially the lighter colors. There are also a lot of colors missing while others come in 10 different shades (no dark brown, but 10 shades of green). But worst of all, quite a few of the pens have different shades on the brush tip versus the regular tip. I like to outline with the regular tip and fill in with the brush tip, but am not able to if the colors don’t match.

I thought if anything the color on the brush would match the fine tips- NOPE. they are drastically different colors. The ink itself is nice but everything else could have been alot better.

Sentence: They are beautiful vibrant colors, and work well.
Content: My kids and I enjoy coloring together and have really enjoyed these markers. They are beautiful vibrant colors, and work well. I just really wish they were labeled with the names of the colors or at least had a number assigned to them so I could make a swatch or something. I feel like I’m guessing every time I pull one out. They are a great price, too!

Content: I have tried several different brands for adult color by number and these are the best. Lots of color variations, love the dual tip.  Perfection!

Sentence: They come with replacement tips, when they get worn and the company out a warranty in the box stating they'll replace the whole pen if they run out of paint.
Content: These are fantastic fine tip and ultra fine tip paint pens. I recently used for several model kits and 3D print projects. They come with replacement tips, when they get worn and the company out a warranty in the box stating they'll replace the whole pen if they run out of paint.

Sentence: All in all, with how many colors you get and the price of them, its a decent value.
Content: Eh its ok. There are some really light colors that dont show up too well. The thin side of the markers are a different color than the brush side. They are not fully opaque and although you can layer them, that doesnt really help. Some thin markers bleed when you color something while others don't. They dry matte which I like and dont come through the other side of any paper. They do have a "medium" drying time compared to other markers i have. I hate that they are not numbered or named because i do a lot of color by numbers and its frustrating to figure that out. Yes, you gwt tiny stickers to put on with numbers but i cant even get the sticker off the sheet! They all rip instead of coming off! All in all, with how many colors you get and the price of them, its a decent value. I've only had them for maybe 2 weeks so I can't speak to durability yet. Guess we will see. (In my picture, the black is the markers, the colors are a gel pen).

Sentence:
Unfortunately, I find that no matter how many layers I do on my coloring page, these markers are VERY streaky.

The brush tips are great and flexible.
Content:
I was really excited to try these because of the dual tips and being able to use the fine tip on tight spaces. Unfortunately, I find that no matter how many layers I do on my coloring page, these markers are VERY streaky.

The brush tips are great and flexible. The fine tip is great for smaller spaces and/or details. The color range is also nice, however, I dislike that they put metallic colors in.

The ink flow is good. It's just so streaky. I end up not using them much and will probably not order them again.
