Sentence: They have such a great selection of colors.
Content: I really wanted to like these. They have such a great selection of colors. However, I notice they aren’t very Opaque for acrylic markers. I have to go over whatever I’m coloring multiple times just so I don’t have to see lines, and this is for both light and dark colors. Some give off more like a highlighter and less than an acrylic markers. I like how they give you extra brush tips which is amazing, but the color payoff isn’t it.

Sentence: The case they come in is outstanding, so well packaged whether it be for doodling , travel, or using in any way.
Content: Welllll, my dearest little doggy chewed up one of my favorite colors and according to the instruction card, they say they will replace damaged or defective markers. So I emailed them for a replacement pen, just the one pen and they sent a whole new box of 120 markers ( which is what I had originally ordered only about 7 days before he had such fun ) !!! Their response time was practically immediately plus they offered a whole new container of 120 pens!!! This is an unsolicited review that just felt I needed to share. Their customer support was fabulous!! So I haven’t had enough time to really make anything yet but I can expand on what I know so far. The case they come in is outstanding, so well packaged whether it be for doodling , travel, or using in any way. Coverage is very good. I am used to another, lacquer medium and was pleased with the ease and coverage. There is a color chart to fill out with the pens. I was surprised at no primary colors, which was no big deal, and except for the metallic pens, all the other colors are a matte, creamy , smooth finish. The pens and packaging, and enclosed literature are very convenient. A note on their note!! It is hilarious to read, they obviously have approached instructions with a touch of humor and it’s entertaining!!! They encourage you to contact them with ANY problems! I’ve enjoyed them immensely!!! Thank you Pagather for a quality product and great customer service!!! I’ll be back for more!! And will include a photo of what I’ve made!!

The more the white touches the dark color even after drying for hours, the tip of the white will eventually be the same as the dark color it’s touching. I don’t want to return them because I have a few projects that I have deadlines on I need to complete without delay of waiting on replacements.

Pros:

- Bright, bold, vibrant, gorgeous colors.

Content:
Absolutely love these. I originally bought the 72ct. After a couple months I decided I liked them well enough to buy the 130ct. For a larger variety.
(First pic is of the 2 sets side by side without the opposite sides of the fold out sections.)

There’s a couple differences between the 2 sets outside of the obvious color range. The 72ct came with just the markers in the case. I expected the same from the 130ct however I was pleasantly surprised to find a baggy of replacement nibs and instructions on how to replace said nibs as well as instructions on how to fix them if they become dried out.

Pros:
- Easy control
- Smooth consistency and flow.
- Juicy
- Bright, bold, vibrant, gorgeous colors.
- If your main qualifier is brush tips these are perfect! Capable of creating thick lines but also capable of creating those fine details as well as get into the smaller nooks and crannies.
- layer well with like colors.
- No smudging or smearing.
- Dry quickly
- Fine tip is great for dotting. I’ve used them primarily for adding dots and other embellishments over top blocks of color.
- Case is well made and makes for easy storage as well as taking them on the go.
- good color variety in both sets making smooth and subtle color transitions a breeze.
- NO BLEEDING

Cons:
- 3 of the markers in the 72ct arrived dry, however not entirely. (Upon receiving instructions in the larger set in how to fix this I feel this has been made up, tho these instructions should be included in the smaller sets.)
- The fine point is not very fine, it is indeed a small bullet tip that doesn’t do well at all for fine details. The brush tip works better.
- There is some color consistency issues between the brush and bullet tip on some colors however slight.
- Some of the fine tips leave behind fibers.
- These do NOT work well on fabrics, colors will not show.
- Majority of the colors do not appear well on black surfaces. (This does not seem to be the case coloring over lines in coloring books).
- Not all colors layer nicely as these are water based, if you attempt to layer colors on opposite sides of the spectrum they just mix.
- There is only one Red in the 72ct.
- Some colors are more transparent than opaque in the fine tip.

Overall, very worth it. I have sets Ive paid more for that were far less quality.

**All NON metallic colors used in my posted photos are from these 2 sets.**

Sentence: It's a really good palette.The brush tips are a joy to use and the paint feels consistent.
Content: Now THIS is a set of acrylic pens! Every set has strengths and weaknesses, so I'm always on the lookout for certain things in particular:- Caps that can be retained on the end of the markers- A set of colors which all have good contrast against one another- Brush tips, so I can do both very fine and very broad strokes with one tip- A good array of DARK colors, not just a good array of midtones and light colors- A good box or case that shows every marker at once and doesn't require lots of searching for an empty spot to put a marker back intoThis set has four of the five things. There aren't many dark colors in here. But I can say that this set has enough color & saturation values for you to be able to make an amazing range of stuff. You can paint things that require lots of fine variations - fancy birds, iridescent bugs, opal, space pictures, and more! There are also a LOT of skin tone options so you can make an accurate likeness of just about anyone. Lots of tan-/dun- like colors for realistic animal fur too. Finally, there are a lot of distinct hues in the red, purple, and pink parts of the spectrum - something I don't see in other marker sets. It's a really good palette.The brush tips are a joy to use and the paint feels consistent. Even the reds and yellows go on very strong, and I don't have to go back over them a lot like I do with other paint pens. In the picture, you can see some doodles I made on a dark rock, and I only had to draw each thing one time to get colors that solid. It's definitely good paint with a lot of pigment in it. I really like the range of color and saturation values on offer because I can use a ton of colors without making something that clashes or hurts my eyes.If you're gonna use or move the box often, I recommend cutting some small holes in the top of the lid. This breaks the vacuum so the lid comes off much more easily.I recommend the pens!

Sentence: Well, the Dual tip is not worth it, imo.
Content:
Tried 3 different sets, these 30 single brush tips and 2 sets of 48 of the dual tipped markers, one from this brand and the other from Pagather that were all in similar price rance during sales. The main question was to see how the brands differed, but also to understand why the dual tip set from THIS brand was so much cheaper despite the additional tip and carry case that these lack. Well, the Dual tip is not worth it, imo. I felt the difference in the weight of the pens, which clearly is due to the amount of LIQUID in them, and these win by a mile. I can see the duals running dry in much less time.

Given the value of how much more coverage you will get from these, this is worth the money where the other is not so much. I easily would choose this set of brush tips only over the dual marker, if only because fine lines are just as achievable with this tip anyway. The fine point of the other is more like a marker than a brush, which maybe is preferable for those without as much motor control in the hands, like kids. But for the price to usage ratio, I think there is much more to found in these.

I am currently considering how much color variety I really need, and whether I am willing to return all three sets to get the 48 single tip markers and case to go with it, or maybe just go with 36 since neither of those is discounted and I don't really NEED this, just thought it might be nice go have as a crafty sort of person who loves art supplies. If I were wanting them for creating paintings myself, I would definitely get the 48 set of these over any of the dual tipped varieties.

If I had these in a zippered case, I wouldn't even think twice about the extra colors and be very satisfied. These seem to be vibrant, more like opaque paint than watercolor, and supposedly waterproof, and seem to have the most favorable reviews with fewer complaints than other brands.

Sentence: They dry so so fast and they don't bleed through your paper, at all!
Content: These acrylic markers are absolutely perfect! They work so well coving the black lines of my coloring books. They dry so so fast and they don't bleed through your paper, at all! For 72 colors, they have a huge variety of colors, making it so easy to add those details to each coloring page. I have tried other brands but these are my absolute favorite! They are extremely affordable for the quality of the markers! If you're debating on these and not sure, let me tell you that you're going to want to order them! They are absolutely worth all the hype! Now that I have them, I can't see my pages without them! The brush tip is perfect, it's great for any size, you can use the tip for smaller areas or lean it to its side and cover larger areas or whatever it may be. All you do is shake the pen & it's already activated, that's basically to make sure your ink is flowing. No pressing and waiting for the ink to come out, it's already ready to use! They are so juicy, too. The ink flow isn't too much or too less, it's perfect! I really believe they are good for all ages, also! I mean clean up is pretty easy, maybe with adults present for younger kids but I believe probably 6plus would fine to use them. I'm in my 30s and I absolutely love them and use them every single time I color. The only thing I wish I would have done differently is get a bigger pack! I hope this helps!

Content:
I’m impressed with the quality and variety of these acrylic markers! They’re the kind you have to prime by shaking and pressing down the nib a few times but they prime much more easily than some so I didn’t find that to be a hindrance.

You get a great selection in this set and most of the colors are very different from each other. The only thing I haven’t had a chance to test so far is how long the markers will last. But with that in mind, they are easy to use and the color goes on super sheer. Between that and the fact that this is the best color selection I’ve found in an acrylic marker set so far, they are definitely worth purchasing.

The price of $52.99 is a bit higher than I’d usually pay (although it’s not a bad deal considering that it’s still less than 50 cents per marker) but the seller is currently offering a 50% off coupon. At that price, this marker set is an absolute steal.

I love that there are glitter, metallic and neon markers included as I don’t often see that with acrylic marker sets — I do wish the glitter shades were a bit more glittery than they are but they’re still nice.

First you have to prime each pen to get the paint flowing. Sentence: The whole set is in a very sturdy box which shuts well with a tuck in lid on top.
Content: I got this set of paint pens because I am going to be doing some acrylic paintings soon and I want to have a variety of techniques available to me.HOW THESE COMEThese come in a clear case with an envelope of paper and swatch sheets.  There are also a few drawing papers to practice coloring on.  The whole set is in a very sturdy box which shuts well with a tuck in lid on top.  This also allows you to store these flat.CASEThe case is clear. Each level comes apart pretty easily.  It has to be laid out side by side for easy access to all of the colors which requires a table top.  To use these on the lap, it is not convenient.  The pens might have to be moved to a holder and then stored flat in the case when you are done.  Alternatively, you can move it to a book style case with pages but remember to store the pens laying flat not end up.PAPERSThe papers inside are excellent quality paper to play around with and do swatches on black and natural light color.  The coloring pages are also really fun to play with.PENSThe paint pens are fantastic.  The brush tips allow for a great flow of paint and it is very close to painting with a brush dipped perfectly.  The colors are painterly vs bright and loud.  The window in the side lets you see how much paint is left.  Since each pen has to be used and covered immediately, I hold the lid while using the pen.  The colors on the end and labeling are well done.QUALITY PAINT AND PERFORMANCEThis is one fantastic set of paint pens.  They paint perfectly and are smooth and have excellent coverage.  There is no skipping and it can go from thin to thick lines pretty easily too.CANVASI used this to test on canvas board and the results were great.  They really look nice on the canvas and dry to nice intense colors.THE BOTTOM LINEThis is a beautiful set of paint markers.  The colors are beautiful and performance is excellent.MY RATINGFIVE STARS.  I like this alot.  The case is a bit tough for me to use in my recliner, but if I move the pens to a book case, it works well.  I just have to remember to lay them flat.  These will also be excellent to do detail work on acrylic paintings and make greeting cards.

Content: UPDATE::: Y'all I love these markers so muchI've been using them consistently since I got them in october- no issues with drying AT ALL, though I would recommend taking them out and giving them a good shake periodically as a precaution.I find that they work smoother/more painterly on canvas or primed surfaces- they dry a bit too quickly on paper and soak up a bit more, but they still didn't even bleed through my mixed media sketchbook, so that's a major win!The case does take up a lot of space when you have all the sections out and accessible, which isn't my favorite, but is only a minor hindrance. No issues with snapping or breaking at all.I still have nitpicks about the color range (lack of oranges and yellows, mostly) but have found that, while they're still wet, they do mix quite nicely. You can achieve a lot of good in-between colors by mixing on the surface you're creating on before the marks dry.Though I am still so sure I will run out of white and yellow before anything else, which has me wishing I could buy individuals.Despite that, these are one of my favorite sets of art supplies in recent years. Content: UPDATE::: Y'all I love these markers so muchI've been using them consistently since I got them in october- no issues with drying AT ALL, though I would recommend taking them out and giving them a good shake periodically as a precaution.I find that they work smoother/more painterly on canvas or primed surfaces- they dry a bit too quickly on paper and soak up a bit more, but they still didn't even bleed through my mixed media sketchbook, so that's a major win!The case does take up a lot of space when you have all the sections out and accessible, which isn't my favorite, but is only a minor hindrance. No issues with snapping or breaking at all.I still have nitpicks about the color range (lack of oranges and yellows, mostly) but have found that, while they're still wet, they do mix quite nicely. You can achieve a lot of good in-between colors by mixing on the surface you're creating on before the marks dry.Though I am still so sure I will run out of white and yellow before anything else, which has me wishing I could buy individuals.Despite that, these are one of my favorite sets of art supplies in recent years. I'm obsessed.Updated pros/consPROS:-Surprisingly opaque-very saturated colors-dries fast and layers well (colors do dry a bit darker, as it goes with acrylic)-The brush tip is actually the best, no more pumping a paint markerCONS:-color range is lacking a bit in oranges, yellows, and dark colors-case takes up a lot of space when opened--------------------------------original review--------------------------------(I got these today, so this is a 'first impressions' review)I'm a artist and art instructor by trade, and I like to use a wide variety of materials to make recommendations to students as well as find new supplies for myself.These markers are pretty solid- I like acrylic paint for its opaque layering properties, as well as the quick dry, and these markers are pretty effective at both. As with acrylic paint, you do have some transparency and a need to layer, especially on lighter colors like white and yellow, or on top of darker colors. But overall, the coverage is pretty solid and the saturation is impressive.The case is a bit weird, you have to be careful separating the layers (they tuck into these little ridges at the back to hold together, and I can see there being a risk of snapping) but otherwise it seems convenient.The color range is odd. Sentence: The pens are ok, but one application didn't cover the black line around the swatch box on the white card, and on the black they were fairly streaky.
Content: The box that these come in is really nice. It's hard plastic, with each tray coming out separately. You can take out one tray, then put the top on that so you have a handle to carry it, so you don't have to take the entire box with you if you don't want to. It's also compact, so it won't take up much room, and the markers can lay horizontally, which is the way acrylic markers should be stored.  I found this box to be the very best feature of the set. I swatched the colors on the swatch sheets that came with it (one white and one black) and I wasn't terribly impressed. The pens are ok, but one application didn't cover the black line around the swatch box on the white card, and on the black they were fairly streaky. I realize that paper isn't the best medium for using acrylic markers (canvas paper, glass and metal would be much better) but I expected the paint to have a little better coverage. I do like that they hold a lot of paint, and that each marker has a number that corresponds with the swatch sheet. I also like the window in the marker that shows how much paint is left, and I really like the brush nib as opposed to hard nibs some other markers have.Do I think this set is worth $69.99?  No. I have other acrylic markers that perform as well, although they might not hold as much paint, and don't have the awesome box. But I'm cheap, so you be the judge.

Sentence: The things that kept me from giving it five stars were as follows: the case is kind of a pain to deal with.
Content: These were really nice paint pens. The things that kept me from giving it five stars were as follows: the case is kind of a pain to deal with. You have to unsnap each layer and lay them all out to have easy access to any color. And then when putting the cases back together you have to make sure that the clip on the case above doesn’t get snapped in when you clip the one below. It just seems very unnecessary when a zipper case that you can unfold and lay out works much better. I have another set of 60 of these almost identical pens and they came in a zipper case that was much easier to deal with. I will say that the case looks very nice tho. My second problem that I took a star off for is that some caps fit nicely in the back of the pen when using it while others were too loose and wouldn’t stay on. I don’t like having loose lids to keep track of and it just seems strange that some would do that while others didn’t.As far as the actual marker goes tho, I would say that they perform at a five star quality. On the swatch sheets I only did one layer for each shade except for the white on the black sheet. I did two layers on that trying to see how many I would need to get a good solid coverage on black. I would say three layers would do it. I don’t ever color on black paper so it’s not an issue to me but that might be a problem covering black lines in coloring books. Rarely would I want to cover a line with white so again that’s fine with me. I also absolutely love the color selection! There are a great range of colors and many neutrals which I appreciate. On white paper it only took one layer for opacity. In fact if you look at the sample flower I painted the darker blue/green outline around the flower had red below it. I changed my mind after coloring it red And then went over with the darker shade of blue/green and it only took one coat to cover the red. I was impressed by that.The presentation of the set was really sharp too! It came with a thick black envelope containing all the swatch sheets, instructions, and sample coloring sheets. Shuttle Art if you’re reading this please make a coloring book specifically using that same white paper and gray outlines for acrylic markers! I would buy that in a heartbeat! I love that paper! Also the case looks really nice setting on your shelf. While I’m not crazy about its functionality it does look sharp and is nice quality. For these reasons I think this set would be a perfect gift for the color lover in your life. It feels a step above the others. Just fantastic presentation.Update: after playing with these for awhile and getting the new pastel set I decided to change the rating to a 5*. The case has NOT been the pain that I thought it would be and for the value of the pens it’s worth it. I would highly recommend these to anyone! Btw if you have the set of 60 and get the pastel set too, the trays DO fit together into one stack. They are a pleasure to color/paint with. 🥰

My second problem that I took a star off for is that some caps fit nicely in the back of the pen when using it while others were too loose and wouldn’t stay on. I don’t like having loose lids to keep track of and it just seems strange that some would do that while others didn’t.As far as the actual marker goes tho, I would say that they perform at a five star quality. On the swatch sheets I only did one layer for each shade except for the white on the black sheet. I did two layers on that trying to see how many I would need to get a good solid coverage on black. I would say three layers would do it. I don’t ever color on black paper so it’s not an issue to me but that might be a problem covering black lines in coloring books. Rarely would I want to cover a line with white so again that’s fine with me. I also absolutely love the color selection! There are a great range of colors and many neutrals which I appreciate. On white paper it only took one layer for opacity. In fact if you look at the sample flower I painted the darker blue/green outline around the flower had red below it. I changed my mind after coloring it red And then went over with the darker shade of blue/green and it only took one coat to cover the red. I was impressed by that.The presentation of the set was really sharp too! It came with a thick black envelope containing all the swatch sheets, instructions, and sample coloring sheets. Shuttle Art if you’re reading this please make a coloring book specifically using that same white paper and gray outlines for acrylic markers! I would buy that in a heartbeat! I love that paper! Also the case looks really nice setting on your shelf. While I’m not crazy about its functionality it does look sharp and is nice quality. For these reasons I think this set would be a perfect gift for the color lover in your life. It feels a step above the others. Just fantastic presentation.Update: after playing with these for awhile and getting the new pastel set I decided to change the rating to a 5*. The case has NOT been the pain that I thought it would be and for the value of the pens it’s worth it. I would highly recommend these to anyone! Btw if you have the set of 60 and get the pastel set too, the trays DO fit together into one stack. They are a pleasure to color/paint with. 🥰

Sentence: If you can't reach into some areas 'cause the tips are too wide, you can then just use a qtip or traditional brush to push the paint into those areas and spread it around.The black pens come in real handy for weathering and fake shadows.
Content: I use pens like these all the time in painting my 3D resin prints. They're great for experimenting 'cause you can try out different colors and color combinations on your prints without having to clean your brushes out each time. You can blend colors together easily on your prints and you can get rid of mistakes just by wiping the paint off. Then, once you get the color scheme you like laid out, you can continue using these pens to apply your final paint job or you can transition to brushes and just use what you just did as a guide.These also work well when it comes to actual painting. You can paint straight areas like pipes and panels and walls with no problem. If you use metallic colors, you can make these things look nice and real. If you can't reach into some areas 'cause the tips are too wide,  you can then just use a qtip or traditional brush to push the paint into those areas and spread it around.The black pens come in real handy for weathering and fake shadows. You can selectively paint over some areas to apply that paint and then just wipe those areas off to leave paint only in the recesses to simulate weathering or shadows. These work great for that.Just be aware that there are limitations with using paint pens like this. You can't easily paint large areas 'cause you'll end up leaving visible pen strokes. You can get around this issue to a certain extent just by gently wiping your painted areas down and applying perhaps more coats. But still large areas could prove difficult.

Sentence: The paint markers come in a sturdy case that snaps shut.
Content:
This is a great set and I started playing with it the day it arrived. The paint markers come in a sturdy case that snaps shut. It's nice that you can see all the markers at the same time. It's a bit tough popping them out, but they stay in place. The lids also securely snap shut but you really have to be sure they are shut -- look at the cap to be sure it's all the way down because it takes some pressure to close them. Because of this, the lids won't fall off.

It comes with a color card so you can test each color and know what they look like, but the layout is confusing and doesn't follow the order of the pens in the case. Why not make them go in the same order? It's very weird but I got most of the colors on it. Still can't find one but eventually I will. The problem is that the paint color is on the top of the cap, so it's hard to see them when the markers are in the case. Also, some are printed in white on light colors so they are really hard to read because they are also very small.  It would be much easier if they were printed on the sides of the pens so you could see them all at once. There is a system to naming them, such as BV1 for blue violet 1. Some of them don't make sense, but most are easy to figure out. Again, all the colors in white on the sides would be a great improvement in the future.

The paint is very nice -- it's really opaque, goes on smooth, and is a bit wetter than typical paint markers like this so you have a bit of time to blend it. Not much, but enough for small areas. You don't have to pump these to prime them as they are ready to go. The tip has a nice flexible point that makes both thin and thick marks really well.

The color selection is what really makes me happy -- this set has not one but two actual REDS! Holy cow, I have been waiting to find a set with red and not some coral/vermillion color pretending to be red. There is a bright red and dark red and they look beautiful. The paint dries darker so don't be fooled by the color you initially see. I was worried the darkest purple wasn't really dark, but it dried to a beautiful dark violet color. The dark brown also dried to a nice deep brown -- another color that is hard to find. I do wish the darkest blue and green were darker, but they're still nice. The green include a light lime green as well as regular grass green, cool greens, olives, and some blue-greens. There is a nice array of purples with warm and cool tones. The pinks are okay -- the dark one is darker than most others I've tried, but still not a true magenta. There is a nice selection of light pinks. The yellows and oranges are wonderful, with shades all the way from light yellow to dark orange and even includes mustard. There are a lot of colors that I would classify as pale skin tones, as well as an array of light to darker browns. There are far more light colors than dark, so this is great if you need pastels. The black is nice and dark with no noticeable cool or warm tones. Overall, I am really happy with the color selection; the cap colors come close to what you actually get.

This set is a bit more expensive than others, but you get so many colors that the cheaper sets just don't have. And the paint is better quality. If you like painting with paint markers, you will love this set.

Content:
I have been collecting a few sets of acrylic marker/paint pents so that I could do some detail work on paintings, models, or artwork and not have to use a brush for some things.

HOW THIS COMES
This comes in a great case. It has a lot of room in it and is very well laid out. They are easy to see and use from a chair or table.

MARKERS
The markers themselves are brush on one end and fine point on the other. There is no window on the side to see the paint level and you do not have to shake them to get them to work.

COLORS
This set has a LOT of colors. If you do anything like rock painting or other bright colored projects, you will have plenty to choose from. Some of the colors are similar, but I don't mind because if one runs out or dries up, I can just change to another.

PERFORMANCE
On paper, these are pretty good intensity. They are not as opaque or thick as some others I have but they still work great for projects that don't need a heavy opaque laydown of paint. On canvas, they are hit and miss. Some of the colors are more transparent than others and will need more coats. The best ones on canvas are the metallics as they cover well and the texture is excellent. I have included a quick photo I took of some tests I ran showing the metallics up close. I hope you can see it.

DRY TIME
These dry very quickly. On paper it is really fast. On canvas, it takes a little bit of time, but not much before you can put on another layer.

USE
You will need to use these. Once you get them, use them. They will most likely dry out pretty quickly and you won't get to have fun with them if you wait too long. This is the type of art tool you want to enjoy when you get it and not put it away for that project you will probably not get to anyway.

THE BOTTOM LINE
For models, artwork, and even rock paintings, these are decent acrylic marker pens. The paints are somewhat transparent in some colors, so plan accordingly

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. For what these are, they are really nice. I love the case and apprecaite how easy it is to see them, store them, and take them with me when I want to do a project. I can do it in a chair or at a table. I just have to remember to push to use them before they dry up at some point so I can enjoy them while they are still working.

Content: Glitter Paint Pens16 Pens0.7 mmFine TipThis is a nice set of paint pens, but I think they are a little misleading. While the paint does have glitter in it, they are actually metallic. I have to take one star off because they are metallic glitter pens. Not glitter alone pens. Oh, and there is no smell at all.

Sentence: Each marker’s ink is opaque, metallic, and glittery enough to blind any dullness in your life.With a 0.7mm fine tip, these markers deliver lines so crisp, you’ll wonder if you’ve secretly become an art prodigy.
Content: Who knew your next masterpiece (or attempt at one) was just a pen shake away? These 16 shimmering colors are here to take your arts and crafts game from “meh” to “wowza!” Whether you’re jazzing up rocks, paper, or random objects around the house, these glitter paint pens will have you channeling your inner glitter god or goddess.From bold blues to radiant reds, these markers scream, “Look at me!” Perfect for crafting, drawing, or doodling on your coffee cup while pretending to take notes in meetings. Each marker’s ink is opaque, metallic, and glittery enough to blind any dullness in your life.With a 0.7mm fine tip, these markers deliver lines so crisp, you’ll wonder if you’ve secretly become an art prodigy. Whether you’re sketching elegant greeting cards or just aggressively doodling glitter mustaches on magazine photos, the ink flows as smoothly as your best pick-up line (or at least smoother).These markers are non-toxic and odorless, so go ahead and let the kids join in—though we can’t promise they won’t cover the walls in glittery doodles (hey, it’s called modern art). The ink is designed to sparkle forever—or at least until your cat decides to knock your project off the table.Don’t panic when nothing happens at first—these markers aren’t broken, just shy. Give them a good shake, press the tip, and voila! Glittery magic. (Pro tip: read the instructions on the box—yes, that box you already threw away.) Once the mystery is solved, you’ll love how easy these are to use.These bad boys write on glass, wood, stone, fabric, paper, and probably that one surface you swore couldn’t be decorated. Turn anything into your personal glittery canvas! Tired of boring notebooks? Done. Want to bedazzle your favorite mug? Go for it. Need to leave passive-aggressive notes on your roommate’s leftovers? Glitter makes it classy.Love the colors, love the glitter, and I’ve left sparkly reminders of my genius on every surface I own.

What I've achieved with this tip is either very fine sketchy lines or blocked in areas of color.What I mean about sketchy lines is that the brush seems to be designed to feel like a paint brush. If you lightly drag the brush across the page you're going to get thin lines, but they aren't going to be consistent. What you get is a thin sketchy line that is fine, but sort of annoying at the same time. I did play with them for a while and after a while I figured out how to use that sketching motion to get some fine points and light lines, but still the ability to paint a long consistent thin line just doesn't really happen or apply here.What happens is if you put the slightest amount of pressure on the tip, you're not really going to get a fine line anymore. The flow of this pen is really good and the paint sort of pools. What you get a thicker line that is very satisfying, and consistent. What I'm used to is a pen that can produce thick and thin lines in the same stroke. With this pen I find myself laying down thick lines, then going back over them and refining the lines to look like it was a thick and thin stroke.My opinion is that it is a good marker. I love the thin body style, and the paint flow is remarkably premium. I love that the set comes in such a nice organizational travel/ storage case and as always Ohuhu's Colors just seem to be so dramatic and satisfying. Actually, I think that is what I like best about this pen. The colors are vivid and beautiful. Compared to other acrylic markers, Ohuhu's colors just seem to pop more, are more precise and opaque on the first coat.On the note of how I feel about the tips?I think I've settled with this marker, I can say that I suggest them but I will also say just be ready for a little bit of a curve ball if you're used to another brand. The brush tips are just slightly different than competitors and maybe you will like them. My conclusion on the tips is that they are niche and have function, I consider it to be a tool whereas because it is different it is valuable. This marker can and does become usable for certain detail situations.Overall, I will say this is a good pen. I think that most people are going to be satisfied with them. I've been a little nit picky about the tips, but I am an artist and things like this that appear to me will probably appear to other artists, so as a reviewer I want to make note of them.Great marker and highly suggested.

Sentence: This would make a perfect Plein Air sketch set, so light and easy to use.Inside, there is a multilingual instruction booklet and 3 swatch cards.
Content: This 24-piece acrylic paint pen kit is a blast--and at a little over $1 a pen, it gives you a lot of entertainment hours for your buck!The set comes in a beautifully decorated hardcover case, with the name "Ohuhu" (leaf in the 'O'), and drawings of leaves, flowers, stars, cactus, a cute gecko, peaceful dove, and other geometrics, designed to inspire, printed on the front in white. The back has Ohuhu's motto, "Draw. Feel. Empower." and a bunch of legal data printed on it. The zipper on the case moves very smoothly, and each pen has its own velcro loop to hold it secure in travel. This would make a perfect Plein Air sketch set, so light and easy to use.Inside, there is a multilingual instruction booklet and 3 swatch cards. 1 swatch card is filled out and has a white background, and there are also two blanks: one white and one black. I encourage you to fill both of these out, first, to prime your pens and get them ready to do an art, and second, so you can notice how the different background colors affect the perceived color of the pens. Even though you are using the exact same color on both cards, the final outcome looks VERY different. After that, you're ready to go!The colors of the paint are opaque, provided you let the bottom colors dry before adding more on top. This takes maybe a minute. You can also blend the colors just a bit by working two colors together quickly, but be careful that you don't foul and muddy your pen tips.Protip: if you've treated your item with gesso (highly recommended), you can blend, work, and even dilute the colors with a damp brush and a little water, allowing you to create watercolor-like effects or blend and smooth sharp lines. The gesso protects your item from the water and smooths the surface in order to accept the paint more readily. It's fairly cheap and available here on Amazon. Think of it as primer, except for art!These pens may not be as versatile as a full acrylic paint set, but neither are they as expensive or as messy. For a more advanced artist, these pens make a great color sketch set so you can get ideas down in the books quickly and conveniently, then you can use your full acrylic or oil paint set to make a full final copy. These paints are great for casual artists or smaller multimedia art projects such as rock painting or just adding a few quick touches to a knitting or sewing project. Not everybody wants or needs to bother with a full paint kit. These pens are also great for card-making and stencils. I'm sure there's a ton of other uses I've forgotten, or don't have the wit to imagine. 10/10, versatile, affordable, and FUN.

Sentence: These pens are very fun to use and have great opacity compared to other acrylic pens I've used.
Content: These pens are very fun to use and have great opacity compared to other acrylic pens I've used. The lines come out crisp and satisfying with good control over the line weight. Unfortunately about half of the pens came partially exploded in the cap. Not a huge deal because they are perfectly functional and the ink spillar was contained inside the cap, but you will want to be careful uncapping them unless you are ok with getting permanent ink splatters on your clothing. The ink does separate when not in use, so you will want to shake them well before using them again. The price is good and the actual ink seems to be good quality even if the pens themselves have some design flaws.

Sentence: Overall, these seem to be quality markers and when these are eventually used up or dry out, we will likely replace them and keep a set around.
Content: I’m not an artist, but we keep some art supplies around for my daughter’s school projects. We tried these out on a coloring page and were pleased with the results. Colors are vibrant and they require no pressure to the paper so it almost feels like painting. These will definitely get use in our house. I also tried these out on an aluminum plant tag. Sharpies do not hold up at all on these metal tags, so now we have a way to use these tags up. Overall, these seem to be quality markers and when these are eventually used up or dry out, we will likely replace them and keep a set around.

Sentence: This is a review for "SHARPIE Creative Markers, Earth Tones, Water-Based Acrylic Markers, Bullet Tip, Assorted Colors, 12 Count, Everything The Light Touches Is Your Canvas, In celebration of Disney’s Mufasa: The Lion King"This set is a compliment to the vibrant set of pens Sharpie released in this new series of paint pens.
Content: This is a review for "SHARPIE Creative Markers, Earth Tones, Water-Based Acrylic Markers, Bullet Tip, Assorted Colors, 12 Count, Everything The Light Touches Is Your Canvas, In celebration of Disney’s Mufasa: The Lion King"This set is a compliment to the vibrant set of pens Sharpie released in this new series of paint pens.  I don't know how this magic works, but these pens do not bleed through paper, yet they very much behave like acrylic paint once they are dry.The pens do not blend very well with each other, so these would be good for projects where you were not trying to create a gradient effect.All of the pen bodies are very well made, the caps are easy to get on/off and the caps to stack or post on the end of the pen.In my opinion, if you could only afford one set of these pens, I would go for the "vibrant" set as this set of earth tones does not give you a rainbow of colors (unless you want an earth-toned rainbow.) There is also no black or white in this set.  This set is a terrific compliment to the vibrant set and the two sets combined, give you a ton of flexibility in creating and coloring.I would describe the tip as a large bullet. These will not be your best option for super small detailed drawing or coloring. They will work wonderfully for larger areas.Three blues, two greens, two purples, one brown, three oranges and a yellow is your pallet.

Sentence: Secondly, not ALL the colors are metallic.
Content: I specifically chose this 72-count set because I am looking for a colors that span the spectrum. This set has numerous colors that are so close they are practically the same, while also completely omitting basic colors. There is not a "true green" in this set. Several teals, two limey greens and a very light mint green, but no basic green. There is an excessive amount of browns- yellow browns, red browns, bronzes, etc.Also, almost all colors have a pearlized, metallic sheen. First, this set was not advertised as metallic. I already have several and was specifically looking for a matte set. Secondly, not ALL the colors are metallic. In general, wouldn't use metallic and not metallic markers together on the same project, so after separating them by finish, I now have two smaller sets of markers with huge gaps in colors. I am not at all pleased. This set was a complete waste of money.As far as the quality of the markers go, they're fine. They all write well. This set should be aimed at small children or people who do not care about color selection.Lastly, the packaging is super flimsy. The marker caps get caught on the paperboard sheets separating the rows, so you have to wrestle the markers out. Also, the carton bows, so the markers bunch together and fall to the bottom of the carton. It's not fun to try to dig them out. I will need to provide my own reusable storage. Would not recommend!!

Sentence: It's not a big issue, but for some reason I like names with the colors.The colors lay down cleanly and I have not experienced any bleed/bleed through from these pens which is really nice.
Content: A nice collection of 48 dual tip acrylic markers that are perfect for your everyday arts and crafts or even the professional. The tips are either a brush style tip or a fine point and with the collection you will receive a small pack of spare tips for both styles. I am not sure how you might replace them as I have not had to do so, but it seems you would simply pull out the old one and place in the new one small end first.One issue I have with these markers is they are not "named" by color. While the caps will indicate the expected color they will lay down, none have a name other than the number on the caps. There is a color card that comes with the pack and you can color in the box for each corresponding pen to know what to expect. It's not a big issue, but for some reason I like names with the colors.The colors lay down cleanly and I have not experienced any bleed/bleed through from these pens which is really nice. The color selection is decent with about an equal mix of darker shades/tones vs lighter ones. I typically prefer to have it skew to the lighter side of the spectrum but these are fine.The brush tip allows you to really vary your lines from as fine as you can make one to a good solid line while the fine tip is just that. I enjoy coloring and creating mandalas, and these work quite well for that purpose. Especially when coloring some of the more intricate designs. Having the fine point allows me to get in the super fine details while not ruining the piece with bleeding/bleed through.The pricing on these is perfect at $15.98 for 48 markers. That really is a good price with what you are getting. These are perfect for the budding artist in your home or for everyday use in projects.

Sentence: As is, 48 dual-tipped markers that work well for around $15 is a good price.
Content: This is a great set of acrylic markers for amateur artists (maybe even professional, which I am not.) There are 48 different colors, with a brush tip on one end and a fine tip on the other. The paint goes down smoothly on many types of surfaces; they worked well for me on paper, glass, and rocks. Each marker is numbered, and they come with a card marked with numbered squares for testing the colors. I colored half of each square with the brush, and the second half with the fine tip, and now I have a great reference card for what each color will actually look like once dry. The set also includes two extra replacement fine tips and two extra brush tips. I have never tried replacing marker tips and I am hesitant to try, for fear of ruining a good marker; but I will try one out if any of the tips become damaged.The markers were not in the box in numbered order when they arrived. I took a few minutes to put them in numerical order, and soon realized that they seemed to be numbered randomly. For instance, one shade of red will not be consecutively numbered next to other shades of red, but instead is randomly placed amongst other colors. So I abandoned the numbering system altogether and arranged them by color.The markers come in a box of thin cardstock that won’t stand the test of time. I would have preferred a sturdier case, but then the price would have had to be higher. As is, 48 dual-tipped markers that work well for around $15 is a good price.

Sentence: Secondly, not ALL the colors are metallic.
Content: I specifically chose this 72-count set because I am looking for a colors that span the spectrum. This set has numerous colors that are so close they are practically the same, while also completely omitting basic colors. There is not a "true green" in this set. Several teals, two limey greens and a very light mint green, but no basic green. There is an excessive amount of browns- yellow browns, red browns, bronzes, etc.Also, almost all colors have a pearlized, metallic sheen. First, this set was not advertised as metallic. I already have several and was specifically looking for a matte set. Secondly, not ALL the colors are metallic. In general, wouldn't use metallic and not metallic markers together on the same project, so after separating them by finish, I now have two smaller sets of markers with huge gaps in colors. I am not at all pleased. This set was a complete waste of money.As far as the quality of the markers go, they're fine. They all write well. This set should be aimed at small children or people who do not care about color selection.Lastly, the packaging is super flimsy. The marker caps get caught on the paperboard sheets separating the rows, so you have to wrestle the markers out. Also, the carton bows, so the markers bunch together and fall to the bottom of the carton. It's not fun to try to dig them out. I will need to provide my own reusable storage. Would not recommend!!

Content:
These pens are similar to other markers, but the acrylic goes on smoothly and dries fairly quickly (not quite as fast as other markers).  The coverage is much better than regular markers and you can fill a lot of space without having to go over areas repeatedly.  It also does not bleed through paper, even lightweight paper.
It may be just a bit messier than some markers because it takes a bit longer to dry, but it cleans up easily with soap and water.

Sentence: Dark colors cover in one coat, while using multiple coats with lighter colors may be necessary to get complete coverage.
Content: Sharpie has yet again created a fantastic product for artists. These acrylic paint markers are ready to use out of the box. There is no shaking the pens or pumping the nibs, which is great. The cardboard box provided is durable and a good place to keep your markers.  This set is priced competitively with the other top brands of acrylic markers.

Sentence: Plenty of colors to choose from and a nice box to hold them in.
Content:
I'm probably using these in a way that most people will not, but they work perfect for my application.  I'm a model railroader and like to customize rolling stock and buildings.  Sometimes I just need a quick bit of color here or there, and to get my paint bottles out, see if I even have the color and go through the process of a quick touchup and then clean brushes, well, admittedly most of the time I simply pass with the idea "I'll get it next time when I need to paint more touchups at once."  Yeah, that never seems to happen.

These have worked perfect for quick touchups or for painting tiny little details.  The kit came with what I consider a broad brush tip and a finer brush tip marker choice.  They work just like a marker, but it's more like paint than ink.  Plenty of colors to choose from and a nice box to hold them in.  The finer tip markers even include white and gray — a very nice touch!

If I had to be picky, the only gripe I might mention is while the caps show the particular color the marker is, it would be nice if the color were larger and even wrapped around the cap.  Trying to find the color I need isn't hard, but not a quick visual reference if you know what I mean.  But that's just me being picky.  One could simply "paint" the color around the cap if it were necessary.

The photo is of a recent project I finished.  The yellow fine-tip paint marker was used to "paint" the steps and ladder on the crane and also the hooks on the boom (boom hooks were then weathered with chalks).  Simple, fast and easy.  No brushes to clean.

Sentence: The water-based acrylic ink flows smoothly, and the colors are vibrant and opaque, even on dark paper.
Content:
I love that this set comes with different tip sizes, so I can experiment with fine details and bold strokes. The water-based acrylic ink flows smoothly, and the colors are vibrant and opaque, even on dark paper. I’ve tried them on paper, canvas, and even wood, and they worked great on all surfaces.

One thing to note is that some colors take a couple of layers to be fully opaque, but that’s expected with water-based markers. Also, shaking and priming the pens before use is necessary, but once you get the hang of it, it’s easy.

Overall, this is a fantastic set for beginners like me who want to explore acrylic markers without spending too much. I highly recommend them for anyone getting into painting or mixed media!

Sentence: PRO's: -good coverage and flow -a nice variety of colors -includes two different tip ends for your needs CON's: -they don't have to be primed, that seems strange to me and I question longevity as well as settling of paint.
Content:
Sharpie is a trustable brand, so I didn't hesitate to order these acrylic markers.  For me, acrylic markers are the perfect supply for rock painting and with a young granddaughter, we do a lot of that around here.

PRO's:
-good coverage and flow
-a nice variety of colors
-includes two different tip ends for your needs

CON's:
-they don't have to be primed, that seems strange to me and I question longevity as well as settling of paint.
-there is only ONE white (bullet tip) my favorite and most used color.  There should be a white in both size tips
-my red had already leaked prior to opening the box
-cost is much higher than comparable sets.

All in all, a 4 star product for me but I will look elsewhere in the future due to high price and non-priming nature.

Sentence: And the colors are vibrant and have great coverage.
Content: My kids and I we do a lot of arts and crafts. And my favorite thing to use is: paint pens, especially since I do a lot of rock painting. And honestly, these impressed me a bit. Also great for writing! I did a quick couple of test rocks to try them out and they are some of the best I have used, they seem like they will last awhile and they don’t seem to run out or dry out quickly, at all. For all the pens, colors, for the price, they are a good value.

Sentence: All the colors were jumbled up and not even in their slots;
Content: First off, I’m pretty sure this was already used before I received it. All the colors were jumbled up and not even in their slots; btw, cheapest quality case, ever.Aside from that, the pens themselves are far from great. They are not really dual tip in the true sense as there is no brush plus fine point. Instead, you get a brush and a broad rounded tip. Although the brush has a reasonably fine point, you cannot do really highly detailed work with these pens. Secondly, the colira(to be fair, this based on only three uses a very small amount) are much duller than many cheaper sets. I used them too so some leaves next to ones drawn with the zscm markers I was hoping to replace. They didn’t compare, completely flat and globular in texture. By way of note, the only reason to replace the zscms was the poor quality of the tips, which come with replacements but not enough.Finally, but again based on only three colors, the palette card is not at all representative of the actual numbered colors.If you want a great set at this price point, buy the chromatek brush markers. No fine point nib, but finer brush head and lustrous colors. These markers are not worth the premium you pay over cheaper sets. These were returned.

Sentence: These are decent acrylic markers, but definitely not professional level artist's paint pens.
Content:
These are decent acrylic markers, but definitely not professional level artist's paint pens. They go on smoothly and dry quickly. No issues with bleeding or smearing, but make sure you give a couple seconds to dry on metal or glass before touching. Each pen has a fine tip and a ball tip (great for doing dots for mandalas). Colors aren't as vibrant as oil markers, on some surfaces colors will be muted. For the purpose of this review, did some dot patterns on wood and many of the purples and pinks looked the same. Layering works great, darker over lighter, but not the other way around. Lighter colors are lost on the darker backgrounds.

Still, these would be great for a variety of crafts and projects. Very cost-effective for kids as well.

Sentence: The sixty markers give you so many colors to work with.
Content: I like the size of this kit. The sixty markers give you so many colors to work with. Notably, there are a few colors so similar they would be hard to tell apart. There is a color chart on the box but I couldn’t find any matching numbers on the markers. I guess it doesn’t matter as you can only use one marker at a time and you have to replace the cap immediately before going on to another color or it could dry out. Most of the caps click shut however, there were a few that did not click though I could tell they were closed tightly. There is a slight smell when used because they are paint. Be aware you have to let first coat of paint dry before applying second coat. It doesn’t even take a minute for it to dry a light coat. They do work on wood, glass, canvas and paper. I haven’t tried any other media yet. I do wish the fine point was even finer for lettering. I am glad I read the product description because I did not realize these markers are supposed to be stored horizontally, so that is a good tip.

Sentence:
simply uncap and go to town
- The caps click when closing so you know it’s firmly capped (some other markers have dried on me when I inadvertently did not put on the caps tight enough)
- While it’s waterproof on surfaces, it washes off clean from your hands.
- Good price point.

So why not 5 stars?
Content:
I am NOT an artist - I am a crafter and, therefore, my review is based on how I would use these paint markers. There’s a lot to like:
- There’s a nice variety of colors though some of are subtle variations
- The bullet (or dot) end is a nice bullet point, which will be good for mandala painting (for me, on river rocks)
- You can get a pretty fine line with the fine tip
- You don’t have to do a lot prep just to get started (e.g., pressing down nibs, waiting for paint to appear, etc.); simply uncap and go to town
- The caps click when closing so you know it’s firmly capped (some other markers have dried on me when I inadvertently did not put on the caps tight enough)
- While it’s waterproof on surfaces, it washes off clean from your hands.
- Good price point.

So why not 5 stars? Well…these might be minor to some, but for me, I was kind of “meh”:
- The colors are in no way labeled. Yes, you can see the color from the cap BUT, as I mentioned, a couple colors are very similar. I swatched all but one pen, but because there’s no number or name, I can’t figure out which one I missed.
- I do like a solid, clicking cap. However, there was an inconsistency - some caps were fine and easy to open; a few were on so tightly, it was a struggle to open. By the time I got one or two uncapped, I was grumpy.
- The coverage is okay, not super-duper. To get a good opaque coverage, you have to wait for one layer of color to dry then go over it. Not a big deal, but the white could be whiter. The silver and gold are nice but my other acrylic metallic markers are more shimmery/shiny. Again, not a bit deal.

Overall, for the number of pens, the quality of the color, and the price point, this is a good purchase - at least from a crafter’s perspective.

Sentence: My last set of acrylic markers would bleed through the pages of my sketchbooks, so I had to keep a page between designs to ensure the markers didn't ruin other pictures.

My last set of acrylic markers would bleed through the pages of my sketchbooks, so I had to keep a page between designs to ensure the markers didn't ruin other pictures. It was a waste of money. These do not do that. They go on more like actual acrylic paint; there is no bleed-through, and the coverage is outstanding. The colors in this are different than the standard colors that are found in other markers, and I appreciate that. Because the coverage is how it is, I'm able to blend colors to reach the more primary colors I usually use without having to waste room on basic colors that can be blended in the box.

I love these colors. I can't tell you how long they'll last yet, but I'm hoping for a long time. I can tell you that I can use light colors over dark colors, and it doesn't ruin the light tip. That's pretty amazing. I am really glad I ordered these.

Sentence: Some of the flowers I colored in and a few of the other designs showed through to the other side of the paper.
Content:
I have a lot of acrylic markers/pens and it would seem like I wouldn't need yet another set, however, so much depends on their tips as to how well they work for what you are using them for. I enjoyed using these markers, but it would be nice to be able to identify each color marker easily.

I appreciate the opportunity to try these markers. Thank you.

Sentence: I love that these are water based and don’t have any strong smell either while using or when dried.

Sentence: The paint is too thin (to help the flow?), flat and chalky.
Content:
I chose this set because I wanted to paint some rocks. I followed the directions and shook each color before use.  The paint is too thin (to help the flow?), flat and chalky. I buy and use a lot of art supplies. I painted the first rock partially white (base for a rocky mountain goat) and after 3 layers the paint is still thin. I painted the second rock black. After letting it dry layer by layer; I started painting flowers on the surface. Again adding 3 or 4 layers to deepen the colors of the petals, letting the paint dry in between. The added colors soaked up the black base paint making the flowers muddy. The end result was a "faded" look.
I painted on paper where it did better.
I would not recommend this paint set if you wanted to use it for anything other than paper - and do not mind the lack of vibrancy, and thinness.

Sentence: I have not used them a lot, so I don't know how long they last.
Content:
I spent many years as a professional graphic, commercial and fine artist, mostly graphic. So my opinion may not really fit with the average person who would use these paints. I think the average person who will buy acrylic paints will like them, because they are used to using acrylics, and are not as picky as I am about precise colors. the paint is acrylic, so it does what acrylic paint does. The best thing about them is The tips. They are amazing. They are not a felt tip, they are a brush tip, so you can make a tiny line by touching very lightly, or wider depending on the pressure you put on the tips, all the way to a really wide line by laying it a little sideways. no need to have double tip, and as far as I can tell, they do not moosh down and loose their sharp point. I have not used them a lot, so I don't know how long they last. The paint dries very quickly, so it will be important to click the lids fully on, each time you quit using one, even for a few minutes.

The reasons I gave this a 3 star rating is that  a) at least one of the most standard colors I would use a lot, and is critical for painting plants or flowers is not included. There is a good light green, but no dark green, and the middle green, is not a good standard green. In my opinion it is a little too blue to look right on green leaves. Unfortunately, you cannot blend acrylics, so you cannot create your own colors, which is why acrylics are not my favorite type of paint. b) these are more expensive than most of the other acrylic paint sets I saw on Amazon, so I don't think it is a good value (one set has 72 colors for about the same price.)

Sentence: I got them to play with in my art journal, and they have been perfect for that use.
Content: I’m very happy with these acrylic paint markers. I got them to play with in my art journal, and they have been perfect for that use. The paint flows out steadily and evenly. The paint can’t be too thick in pens, or it wouldn’t work, but the paint isn’t so thin that it’s transparent. I feel like this set of acrylic markers is a fabulous bargain at the current price of $15.99. I very highly recommend them.

Sentence: These markers are vibrant, smooth, and packed with ink—no weak streaky lines here.
Content: I received this set of paint markers for free through the Amazon Vine program, and I’ve been happily doodling on everything that’ll sit still long enough. These markers are vibrant, smooth, and packed with ink—no weak streaky lines here. Whether I’m decorating a notebook or turning a boring stone into a tiny masterpiece, they handle it like champs.They work well on a surprising number of surfaces—paper, glass, pottery, even the random seashell I found in a drawer. The ink dries quickly and doesn’t smear, which is ideal for impatient artists (like me) who inevitably poke at their work too soon. I also appreciate that there’s no awful chemical smell, so I can craft indoors without worrying about fumigating the place.If you’re looking to add a pop of color to your next creative project—or just want an excuse to draw on things like a grown-up child—this set is a fun and easy way to do it. Bonus: now my rock collection has more personality than some people I know.

Sentence: Overall these are priced well, have dual tips and vibrant colors.
Content:
If you never tried paint markers then these are the ones for you. I have a few different sets from other brands and I will say this set is by far the best. Not only are there a bunch of great colors in the set but having dual tips is really great. I love having the brush tip as well as the firm tip. Depending on what you are making each tip will come in handy.

The set of colors you get is fantastic. You of course get the basics but then you get lots of other hues to really make this a well rounded set not only for beginners but to pros as well. These can be used on fabric, paper, wood and rocks as well as other materials like glass and plant pots but I definitely recommend that most of these get sprayed or coated with some kind of sealant especially if used outside or around water. These are just acrylic markers and they will fade, chip etc depending on what was painted. So example, if you paint a rock, spray it with clear coating.

The tips are smooth and the paint goes on easily. They never drip, splat or clog. Colors are vibrant and have a great opaqueness to them so you don't have to layer to cover. However, depending on the material you use , you may have to apply a second coat.

Overall these are priced well, have dual tips and vibrant colors. definitely quality markers.

Sentence: She is a huge fan of a youtuber that I won't name, but this youtuber introduced my daughter to an expensive product that she loves to use frequently: the Posca paint marker.
Content:
My daughter the aspiring artist is constantly working on some sort of artwork or craft project. She is a huge fan of a youtuber that I won't name, but this youtuber introduced my daughter to an expensive product that she loves to use frequently: the Posca paint marker.

Posca makes (as far as I know) the premiere go-to paint marker and they are not cheap. When I saw these being offered, I figured they were worth giving a try and worst case scenario I figured I could at least convince her to use these less expensive markers on her less important projects or for "practice" before using the pricey markers. Either way, when I gave these to her she was much more excited than I expected and was very happy to have this new big set of markers.

She used them for the first time not too long after she got them and loves them. She says they are almost exactly like her Poscas and likes that these have different tips on each side. She said she still prefers using the Posca but that these are really close. Myself, looking at things she has used the markers on, I really can't tell any difference in quality of the paint itself. It looks vibrant and bold.

Honestly I can't think of any negatives to mention. These are high quality paint markers that work well and look great. The price point is excellent compared to premium brands with the product itself performing just as well. Highly recommend to
artists and other parents of artists.

Sentence: Overall, the pens are a joy to use.
Content:
As long as you shake these paint markers before using, they work great. I love that you can layer light colors over dark ones. I am extremely sensitive to chemicals, and these have nothing in them that triggers my allergies.

They have two tips, a blunt one for wide strokes and a pointy one for variable line width. I personally could not control the line width of the pointy tip, but I imagine that someone with good fine motor control could. So it's not really great for super detail work, because if you accidentally press a little too hard, the pen will create a wide stroke instead of thin.

There are just a couple of minor things I think could have been designed better. To tell which tip is which without removing the caps, you need to read the fine print on the middle section of the pen. It would have been nice if they made the caps different to make it more obvious. Also, the box doesn't work great for storage. You have to dig around to get the pens out, and they don't always go back in easily.

These detractions are minor. Overall, the pens are a joy to use.

Sentence: Only one of the colors required a little touch up in my swatch book to get full coverage.
Content:
I'm normally a brand snob, enjoying only the finest of my curated art tools and wanting nothing but the best for what I create in my sketchbook. However, even though I hadn't heard of this brand before, I was really surprised by the quality of their markers. Compared to POSCA and Arrtx, these are closer to POSCA in terms of vibrancy. They pop off the page, plus they went on very smooth and opaque. Only one of the colors required a little touch up in my swatch book to get full coverage.

One huge selling point (and a gripe I have about most brands of markers/pens) is that these markers are labeled/numbered on both ends. Again, this is huge. I never understood why Arrtx made you put stickers on their paint markers and try to eyeball which sticker went with which color. I very much appreciated Betem's simple design here and the ease of use to quickly identify what each color is, whether the marker is up or down.

This allows laying a lighter color over a dark color, within a minute or so of applying the dark color.  The dual tip is helpful and protects the fine point, when you need to lay down a block of color.  I did this mini 3x3” painting of my cat.  But I would expect these to be most used as detail work on a larger image or for crafting.  These are not viable for blending.  So, my only request is more colors.  This set has 36 colors.  I want 144, or more.

Sentence: I really like that They have a paintbrush flexible tip as well as what they call a fine tip however, I would call it more of a medium tip.

Sentence: The pens are comfortable to hold and use.
Content: I ordered this paint pen set for the wide assortment of colors. I have other sets, but their colors are limited, especially with the pinks and greens. This set has an excellent selection and even some metallic colors, too. The pens are comfortable to hold and use. I prefer the round barrel than the square shape with rounded edges (like my other sets). I have more control with this set. Even though they don't have to be prepped before use, when you first use them, the paint is a bit lighter and gets a richer hue as you make more strokes. The coverage is pretty good, but you may need to go over your area more than once to get full coverage. I tried them on an unpainted vinyl doll head and a foam clay flower, and both pieces received the paint very well, but I did have to keep applying paint here and there to get a good coating. Overall, they're nice for hobbyists and crafters, but may not be up to professional standards. They come in a securely sewn storage pack that has a smoothly functioning zipper. The set doesn't have names or numbers for the individual pens, so it could get confusing trying to remember which shade you are supposed to be using. It would be much better if they were numbered, but it's a nice set and I recommend it for amateur artists, crafters, and as a much cleaner alternative to traditional paint and brush setups.

Now, I am not gonna sit here and say these are the most high quality markers I have ever used, but I will still say they are good quality. When I say they are good quality I mean the quality of these exceeds the price that they are. They are absolutely worth the money and I am super happy with these. The colors are beautiful. While some of the colors are not as vibrant as I would hope, overall they are still pretty nice colors and again, these are a cost effective option, so they are not going to be the most perfect marker ever. They look great and are not streaky or ugly. The pens do not dry out easily so as long as you treat them well, they will get a lot of use and have a long life. They are super easy to use. Perfectly functional markers with really no glaring issues. I didn't have any issues with bleed through either. While they are not the most perfect markers ever, for the amount that you get, the price, and the presentation I would say they are well worth the price. Absolutely worth the price and I would think most would love these. Great for kids or teens, they will be super happy with them.

Sentence: However, there are some issues that really brought the rating down.For one thing, I had one marker completed dried out.
Content: I wanted to give these four stars. After all, it’s 240 colors at a very fair price and the paint and color range is great. However, there are some issues that really brought the rating down.For one thing, I had one marker completed dried out. It was a fairly important one for the type of work I do but at least there are a few similar colors and 1/240 isn’t horrible.For another thing, some of the caps have dark writing on a dark cap so I have to really strain my eyes to see the numbers. Sometimes it’s so bad I have to use my phone’s flashlight to see what the numbers are. I wish they’d used white on those like they did most of the dark lids. I don’t know why they failed to do so in so many colors.The thing that bothers me most about the set is that the color numbers are totally out of order on the swatch card. So even if you manage to put them in order you’d never be able match them up quickly to the card. It took me about FOUR HOURS to swatch them all because I had to search and search for the appropriate number on the swatch card for every single marker. Why on earth couldn’t they have put them in numerical order on the swatch card or just given us an un-numbered card so we could write them in ourselves? This is the issue that lost them the star for me. It’s really, really frustrating.Overall it’s a beautiful set, but because of the swatch card issue I’ll have to totally redo the ordering of my entire set to try to put them into an order where I can halfway match them to the swatch sheet. What a hassle.

Sentence: If you want to make the sheet easier to access markers from, you will need to put them in order yourself.SWATCH SHEETThankfully this comes with a really nice heavy duty paper swatch sheet.
Content: I have had a need for acrylic markers.  Everyone in the family has different things they are doing, but I prefer we all have our own sets to use.  I got this one for our son who wanted a complete set for his 3D gaming projects which are extensive and intricate.BOXThe box with this set is GREAT.  It is a not hard to get the markers out, but they are not in order which makes doing the swatch sheet annoying and frustrating.  If you want to make the sheet easier to access markers from, you will need to put them in order yourself.SWATCH SHEETThankfully this comes with a really nice heavy duty paper swatch sheet.  It allows for really good swatches to be made for reference.MARKERSThe markers do not have color names, but each cap is marked with the color number.  There is a window in the side which allows you to see if the paint needs mixing, or if the levels are getting too low.  You can shake each one easily side to side, just don't go nuts with it.LEAKAGE?There was no leakage with these markers.  Flow was even and nice for almost all colors.COLORSThis is the most complete set of colors I have ever seen.  It is really nice and covers any type of project you can imagine.TIPSThere is a bag of replacement tips if you need one.PERFORMANCEThe performmance of these markers is really nice.  The colors are pretty decent, the application is smooth, and it allows for fine details or broader coverage.  I like these on paper and canvas a lot.  I am not as fond of them on glass or smooth plastic.  They tend to chip or scratch off if hit just right.ONE ISSUEI had no colors missing, but one of the colors has the tip put in backwards.  I haven't had the opportunity to change it around yet.THE BOTTOM LINEThis box is great, the swatch sheet is great, and the markers/pens are good performers.MY RATINGFIVE STARS.  This set of markers is a great collection.  None of th pens were dry, all of them worked well, and with the exception of the upside down tip they performed very well.  I highly suggest these, ,but use testing before doing a project to see how well it lasts on the surface you intend to use.DOES HE LIKE ITOur son really loves this set.  He is already opening up his 3D gaming manufacturing for his projects and enjyoing the flexibility that it allows for his textured plastic pieces and landscaping set ups.

Sentence: Each stroke is very pigmented and not streaky!
Content: These markers are crazy! They start out as regular marker ink and then they dry as paint. It’s like painting without the mess. The price point for 240 good quality paint markers is good. Sentence: Set of 240 acrylic brush markers with bright fresh colors, smooth flow, and a window to show how much pigment is left.
Content: Set of 240 acrylic brush markers with bright fresh colors, smooth flow, and a window to show how much pigment is left. Includes a swatch card on Cold Press card stock, which is great except the numbers are chaotic. You have to do a 'Where's Waldo?' search for each number to match them up. It's probably easier and faster to use a blank sheet to swatch them, although you may not need swatches since you can see the color on the bristles when you open the cap.Great range of colors, which is helpful because acrylic brushes dry fast and aren't as easy to blend as watercolors or tube acrylics.The price is about $0.50 per pen and sometimes less when they have discounts.Very versatile and fun to use. You can paint on almost anything... stones, glass, plastic, rocks cardboard, metal, paper... just remember to shake them well first. My only complaint is the order of the numbers on the swatch card, but it's not concerning enough to take off a star. The paints themselves are good.
