Sentence: The quality is what I'm concerned about and I have yet to test to see if they are really waterproof.
Content: I love the variety of colors this set of brush acrylic markers offers. I've been using paint pens or acrylic markers for about 7 or 8 years. I used to buy them individually and pay through the nose. Then I started looking on Amazon because my granddaughter requested acrylic markers for Christmas. She loved mine and is my up-and-coming little artist. When I found the markers she requested and bought them I got to play with them too. They were great I wanted more. And I bought a few different brands that I say the quality is probably just as good as these are however I paid a lot more to get a lot less. And with these markers the variety is outstanding I'm always looking for more earthstone colors and different shades of red yellow green and brown.These markers are great. A rival to any high dollar marker set out there like Posca. You will have to have an outline marker because these are all brush tips. And I haven't found that they have any hard tip markers from 1 mm through 3 mm. Only the brush tip. But you can do so much with these and they are wonderful. They also supply you with extra tips which is phenomenal. So far I have enjoyed these markers. They do not come in order with the swatch card that they provide. Which was kind of a pain in the butt. However that's just a tiny little complaint. The quality is what I'm concerned about and I have yet to test to see if they are really waterproof. But I have another statue to paint and several signs to repaint that have been sun bleached over the years. So I will update if I need to on how they last outdoors. I have submitted a small cartoon that I sketched & painted just for this review, with the number markers provided. Just to show you how true the colors are. I am very pleased and excited to continue on my paint marker journey. And can I just say for the record paint markers are the best thing since sliced bread. They have changed the game. Well done thank you!

Sentence: The colors are vivid and there is pretty much every color you can think of.
Content: This is a beautiful set of paint markers. My daughter's and I have been using them every day since they arrived. All 3 of us took turns doing the swatches. Which was actually really fun - and a bit stressful at times.The numbering system of these paint markers is an absolute atrocity lol. I didn't remove any stars for the numbering because the markers themselves are great.The colors are numbered - from 600's - 900's. 6 and 9 are the two worst possible numbers you can use for a numbering tangible items. It's so easy to conflate one for the other. Some of these pens caps had little dots on them (either above or below the 6 or 9?!) since no one knows if the dot indicates up or down/top or bottom, it's essentially just a useless decorative mark above or below a 6 or a 9 lol.About halfway into the color chart, I started to see a pattern and deduced that the colors seem to be more organized by their secondary tones/color temperatures as opposed to primary. I also realized that most are grouped into similar colors, so you can look in the same color family as the previous one for the next number. However, when a new undertone section starts, you won't know - and good luck finding the numbered pen you're looking for at that point haha.Aside from the numbering nightmare lol, these are perfect. Every single one worked flawlessly and had a great flow. The colors are vivid and there is pretty much every color you can think of. I did notice that a few tips were more flexible than others. I definitely prefer the firmer ones are they are easier to control for smaller designs - which is mostly what I do.  This set also includes extra tips - which is appreciated.If your planning to buy this set of 240 paint pens, keep an eye on the price. When I acquired this, it was selling for close to $150. At the time of this review, it's selling for $118. If you break it down, it's like 50¢ per marker. Which is pretty reasonable compared to Posca. I think this set would make an awesome gift for anyone who loves art. My teenage daughter's and I have been painting rocks with these and they work beautifully for it. But there are so many applications for these besides just rocks. We are very happy with them and although the color swatching was a bit maddening, I really did enjoy the challenge of it.

Sentence: I would definitely see this as an investment at this price, I feel it's a really good price for what you're getting.
Content: I would definitely see this as an investment at this price, I feel it's a really good price for what you're getting. There are 240 acrylic markers in the set, so be prepared to spend some time getting them in order, because they do NOT come that way. Also, the numbers do not make any sense at all! There are some hundreds apart and then you'll come across the rare gem with a few in order (very few!)... But a treat when you're sorting this many. But it would be nice if these numbers meant anything at all versus the randomness that exists. I got over that annoyance, at least a little, by the fact that the lids are a very close match, if not exact, to the color you'll get on the swatch card. That's refreshing! There were only a few things I found during my long swatching and reorganizing session and those were as follows: 1) I found a weird black substance on one of the pens and later on the paper when one of the pieces fell off. No idea what it is, but it's pictured, 2) there was a visible "division" or splitting of the paint in the window of one of my markers. I don't know if it matters or if it's all mixed up in the end when you shake the pen each time?, 3) I had the felt from the end come off a few times while marking in the little swatch box. I can only imagine what this would do on a rough or large surface!! On one it came off in little pieces and ended up in/under the paint causing it to be all bumpy (see arrows in pic). The other few times it happened it was all one piece and while it did dull the tip slightly, it wasn't a huge enough chunk to make a big difference., and 4) the annoyance that this large set of 240 markers didn't come with a better divided box. It has thin dividers that are barely held in place by a notch and mine is broken. I don't know if it was already like that, but I don't know of it happening that I was aware of. It just makes it even harder to keep the pens in place while trying to sort them. And because they don't have they're own individual spot (or at min. their own rows) they move around every time you take one out, therefore causing a bit of an ordeal **everytime** you remove a marker and go to put it back in. This would've been eliminated had these been in a case where each marker has it's own spot. I don't need a headache each time I use these and I can see this making me not want to deal with them and choosing one of my other sets instead. Overall I think it's a good buy, but with 240 chances for something to go wrong, I only had a handful, so that's good. I felt it was worth about 3.5 stars sure to the issues (the biggest deduction because of the box not being properly divided bc it is a huge hassle) but since I can't do that, I gave 4.I tried to be as thorough as possible and include pictures so you could see for yourself what you'll receive (or potentially in the case of issues... Hopefully those are left out of your order!;)) But I hope you found it helpful. Take care and happy creating & painting!

Sentence: They're really juicy, but don't leak all over your work.
Content: I love these paint pens!  They're really juicy, but don't leak all over your work. There are so many colors! Of course when you get as large a selection as this, there's bound to be a few that are too close to tell them apart, but you'll find that in most large quantity paint pens. I really like the brush tip, and the free ink system. You do have to shake them before using, but that's a small thing. Most are quite opaque, with only a few of the lighters colors needing 2 coats. They go on smoothly, and I can use colored pencils easily on top.  Here's the con.... they come with a swatch sheet, which I always fill out whether it's markers, pencils, paint, etc., but this one was a real trial of my patience. The numbers were not in order. For instance on row one, the numbers are730.700,648,727,647, and they aren't on the swatch sheet by color either. So  you pull out a pen then hunt through 240 tiny boxes to try to find where it goes. It took me a few mind numbing hours to get them all swatched, then I organized them the way I wanted. Besides that, I enjoy using them. The box is sturdy, but the separating 'cubes' even though quite thick, can break easily from the weight of the pens when you store them on their side like you're supposed to. The colors are rich and well, colorful. lol  At about $.45 per pen, they're a really good buy. I'm not a professional artist, so they might find them lacking for one reason or another, but for my needs, they're great.

Sentence: Streaking or bleeding can be caused by the ink or paint settling on one side or the other.
Content:
Definitely get these if you want an high-quality beginner’s set of acrylic markers…you just can’t beat this price for the quality and variety of markers you receive!!

**IT IS VERY IMPORTANT that you STORE THESE MARKERS ON THEIR SIDES AND FLIP THE CASE OVER EVERY WEEK OR SO** this tip is for ANY art markers. Streaking or bleeding can be caused by the ink or paint settling on one side or the other. Particularly if these have been stored vertically in the warehouse. For dual end markers, always store the case so that the markers lay on their side, and the flip the case on its other side anytime you think about it.

Do some test swatches and practice drawings before starting on your final project. This way you understand how these particular markers perform. If you’d re having a problem with streaking, lay the case on its side overnight, and also flip the case to the other side for the next morning, then try again. Usually solves the problem with new markers!

Yes, the individual markers *don’t* come labeled with numbers or color names, BUT they come with a chart to assist and have colored caps at both ends. When you think of how many countries (with different languages) they have to ship these to, I think this plan makes sense.

Don’t mix up the caps! But it’s also a good reminder to instantly replace the caps after you use a specific marker….you DON’T want to leave the caps off of acrylic markers longer than you have to in order to color with them.

Also consider the cost savings of not labeling each individual marker….savings that got passed on to us!

I’m impressed with the case quality. I received a different case of markers from another brand, and that case was very flimsy—not this case!!

This is a great deal for good quality markers. 5/5

Sentence: There isn't a bad smell to the markers that you sometimes get with these types of paint pens so you can go extended sessions of coloring.
Content: These markers are great. The chart has names and numbers, but there’s no markings on the paint pens themselves - kinda pointless and you have to just go by the cap color. As long as you have a chart and keep them in order I guess it’s not that bad, but what if you take multiple out or use different storage? When swatching them, I noticed that some are nice and “juicy” where the paint flows nicely, but others are dryer, and you’ll need to go slower to get better coverage. The paint is on the thinner side, so they can get a little streaky, and the opacity just isn’t there. The dark colors are obviously better, but mid tones (like red) didn’t cover black ink, even with three coats, and some of the dark colors (like dark green) failed here, too. Personally, I prefer opaque paint, but this might not be a negative for some. Of the colors, I do think there’s a nice selection of warm, cool, a couple of skin tone, and neutral colors, and even a handful of metallic. For a beginner set, I think there’s colors are good to get started for sure.

I plan to play around with them a little more, but I think this set will get passed along to the kids for their projects and play. For the current price, they’re worth checking out, and would make a good gift for kids. If you are familiar with some of the more expensive brands of paint markers though, I would probably skip these. It just depends on what you want them for.

Sentence: But they did hold in place until putting them out, so not too difficult to keep organized either.They are not "cheap" in terms of total cost.
Content: I do a lot of painting - across lots of media.  I paint wood, canvas, fabric, stone, shoes, clothing, hats, metal plates. . .To be fair, I have not tried these on all of those yet - and I would probably wait for a few until I get a really good fixative. . . But I have tried quite a few of the colours and. . .they are surprisingly bright and vibrant - even on the wood.  They bonded well so far with: wood, the plastic, canvas, and fabric.  The tips are small enough to get a decent amount of detail - assuming you have a decent to better than average steadiness in your hands.  There are an insane amount of colours - some more subtle and some incredibly different - I'm still playing around to figure out which to use for what, but I did appreciate the fact they included a few little boards that you can effectively use as test swatches for the colours (though. . .you could just use scrap cardboard or whatever you have on hand. . .but still nice).The case holding it is nice.  Simple unzip, and the markers essentially just cascade and unfold - and as I noted. . .there are a lot.  But they did hold in place until putting them out, so not too difficult to keep organized either.They are not "cheap" in terms of total cost. . .but when you consider you are getting over 200. . .the price actually seems pretty fair, too.  Once I get a protective fixative to test on it, I could say more, but right now. . .these are pretty great.

Sentence: There is a LOT of colors to choose from for whatever you'll be using them on.
Content: This is a BIG set of markers so be prepared. I didn't realize this until they showed up but this is a good thing. There is a LOT of colors to choose from for whatever you'll be using them on. The markers look and feel great in your hands. The caps snap on/off securely and no worries of them coming off on their own. The colors are rich and dry pretty quick as well. There is also extra marker tips that come with this set in case you tear up a tip (coloring on rough wood or something) and there's a marking chart to test your colors on too. Our daughters and myself have had a lot of fun with them already and we've only had them a day so far.

Sentence: The marker nibs work well, but after a bit of use start to get flimsy at the tip.
Content: I am really liking this acrylic paint marker set. I really like the many, many different colors that you receive in this set. The colors are vibrant and color smoothly. They do include 20 replacement tips so that when they start to get mushy at the end, it can easily be fixed without losing an entire marker. This is a pricey set, but I love the versatility this provides with the smooth coverage and color options. I would definitely get these again.

Sentence: I love that the markers do not bleed through on thin coloring books.
Content: These markers are worth their value. I like how every single marker has its own elastic band. When the set first came in, all of the markers were not in order, so while I was filling in the swatch card, I put the markers into the order that matches the color cards. I also gave each row.A label by using the white marker. I recommend actually taking the time to do this step. It will make it easier for you when you're trying to find a specific color based on the color card.I have used these markers so far on paper on cardboard, on plastic and on leaves and they work as if I was coloring in a coloring book. I love that the markers do not bleed through on thin coloring books. The pictures i'm showing are of a color by number coloring book. I wanted to use this one so you can see how well the colors cover the printed letter or number. The majority of the colors do cover the black font of the number/letter code in the pixel boxes. There are only a small handful of colors that you may need to layer up. A perfect example is the wheat color in the photos. The set comes with twenty extra nibs, so if you find a marker's nib gets frayed, you can replace it. The zippered bag comes in handy too. It makes the markers easier to lug around, to store away, and is more appealing than a box of markers.

Sentence: The clever design of the box, which functions as a sturdy carrying case with dividers, is an excellent touch.
Content:
From the moment I unboxed this marker set, I was impressed. The clever design of the box, which functions as a sturdy carrying case with dividers, is an excellent touch. It keeps the markers organized and prevents them from rolling around—a small detail that makes a big difference. I immediately put these pens to work, using them to add detailed embellishments to my epoxy crafts and to sign my acrylic artwork.

What truly stands out about this set is its thoughtful design and fantastic performance. The markers are a comfortable size, and I appreciate being able to see the ink levels clearly. They were ready to use right out of the box; all it took was a quick shake, and they were working perfectly. The pack also comes with extra tips, and I found the fine tips to be incredibly versatile—perfect for creating both crisp, thin lines and filling in larger areas. On top of all that, the set includes a wide and vibrant range of eye-catching colors that really make my work pop.

The only real drawback I found was the drying time, which takes about 5 minutes for the ink to fully set. When I was layering multiple colors in a single design, I had to be patient and wait between applications to avoid smudging or bleeding.

Overall, this is a great set that I would recommend to both beginners and advanced artists or crafters. The vibrant colors also make them useful for everyday tasks like labeling and organizing around the house or office. It’s a versatile and high-quality product, as long as you're prepared for a little extra drying time when working on intricate, multi-layered projects.

Sentence: On paper and canvas I get crisp lines in 1 coat.
Content:
I have had this set for 20 days and it has pulled its weight on a bunch of projects. First stroke out of the cap was clean with no shaking or priming. The brush tips feel springy and make thin outlines or solid fills without fighting me. Coverage is strong. On paper and canvas I get crisp lines in 1 coat. On plastic and a dark river rock I needed 2 quick coats, and the second went on soon after the first without lifting the color.

I tested a handful of surfaces. Cardstock, canvas panel, a 3D print, a glazed mug, and a few garden stones. The ink flow stayed even and I did not see sputtering. On glass labels the writing stayed put through dry wiping and light scratches. It lifted with a wet paper towel, which is actually handy for temporary kitchen labels. Once fully dry on the rocks and mug it held up to a rinse in cool water.

The color range is generous. Most hues pop and layer well. A few shades are very close, so I filled in the swatch card and put tiny dots on the caps to speed up picking the right one. Dry time depends on the surface. Paper was touch safe in about 2 min. Smooth plastic was closer to 5. The see through ink window is useful, and the divided storage box keeps everything tidy in a backpack. Extra tips are a smart bonus.

For the size of the set and how reliably these write, the value feels excellent. Easy start, bright results, and dependable control across materials. I reach for them now when I want paint look with marker speed.

Sentence: 2 thick layers was much better, almost completely opaque.
Content:
I ordered these markers for the purpose of decorating smooth rocks. I am not a crafty person so I don't know if I am supposed to prime/seal/coat/etc a surface like a rock before painting it, so I didn't. I just drew directly on the rocks.

The  rocks were about 2" in diameter. I found the fine tip end to be good for more precision drawing or for writing. The blunt tip end was good for coloring in designs and whatnot.

My rocks were a light tannish-grey color. I colored one completely white so I could draw on a white surface. 1 basic layer had pretty good coverage, but you could still see the darker tint of the rock beneath. 2 thick layers was much better, almost completely opaque. I probably could have gone a little lighter handed, but while the blunt tip is good for general use I feel like I needed a wider tip to color the entire rock evenly. You can faintly see marker lines. If  I was coloring a smaller rock it probably would be quick and thorough work.

I found that in general I needed more than 1 coat of the paint coloring over the rocks described above. 1 coat of paint goes on rich and bold, but as it dries it fades. I can see how precisely adding additional coats could be difficult for tasks such as writing or fine lines. I'm guessing this is due to the paint seeping into any micro cracks and holes in the rock surface, so in hindsight priming the rock first is probably the way to go to save yourself from using a lot of paint, as well as coloring over lighter surfaces.

I am glad I ordered them for my project and am satisfied with the turn out. I also appreciate the convenience and lack of mess that can accompany traditional painting.

Sentence: These acrylic markers are perfect for painting on glass, wood, ceramic, pottery, leather, fabric, plastic, and even rocks!
Content:
I love to get creative and paint on all kinds of different surfaces. These acrylic markers are perfect for painting on glass, wood, ceramic, pottery, leather, fabric, plastic, and even rocks! I feel like I can use these markers on pretty much anything.

This is a decent set of 24 really pretty, vibrant colors, including all the primaries, secondaries, and some metallics. The pens have dual tips, one larger bullet-shaped tip, and one smaller pointed tip. They are great for dot-painting, as well as for lines, color fill, and intricate details. It’s easy to layer colors on top of colors because they are opaque (like I can apply yellow on top of blue). Plus, the bright colors really pop on darker backgrounds.

They’re fade-resistant and waterproof, too, which works great for glassware and ceramic dishes that will be washed (I can apply a spray sealant on top for extra protection). The paint covers well and dries fast. They are a nice alternative to water-based or alcohol-based markers because they are so versatile. This is a great set for anyone with a creative streak – kids or adults alike!

Sentence: The fine nib had a structure that was rigid enough to produce letter-weight lines on paper, but it was also flexible enough to glide over the uneven surface of river rock.
Content: After completing a single project, it will become second nature to grip the correct side of the barrel since it specifies both tip sizes on each barrel: 1 mm fine on one end and 1-5 mm dot on the other. It just took a few fast shakes and a little squeeze for the color to flow evenly on the very first attempt. The fine nib had a structure that was rigid enough to produce letter-weight lines on paper, but it was also flexible enough to glide over the uneven surface of river rock. By switching to the dot tip, I was able to create smooth circles that could be broadened or narrowed depending only on the amount of pressure used, which eliminated the need for me to search for toothpicks and ball tools. A real carbon black, delicate pastels, shiny gold, and sharp primaries are all included in the palette this time around. On a canvas panel that had been primed, the colors dried to a satin finish that was uniform throughout, with no patchiness or edge bloom. It was shown that the binder is able to adhere to surfaces rather than float on them by the fact that metallics maintained their shimmer on both polished glass and porous terracotta. Two coats were required to obtain full opacity on slate coasters; yet, after a single pass, the fabric absorbed just enough to provide the look of a vintage wash. This adaptability was something I did not anticipate from a single ink formulation.

Sentence: This demonstrates that the pigmentation is robust enough to stand on its own rather than only serving as accents, since even the lighter colors, which are often weaker in other markers, covered the black glass with confidence.
Content: I noted how consistently the ink flowed the instant I opened the black fineliner and drew a delicate vine over river stone. There was no spatter at the beginning, and there was no unexpected fade midway through a curve. Simply giving the tip a little shake was all that was required to prime it, and after that, the line density remained consistent throughout the whole process. During the process of filling the petals, the accompanying dot tip came into action; a small touch resulted in precise polka dots, while a heavier press resulted in significant circles that were ideal for the centers. Changing the tips of your pencil in the middle of a stroke is as natural as switching between different grades of pencil, but there is no need to roll around the table looking for a third pen. It would seem like a little spread to have twenty-four different hues, but when it is stacked, it really amounts to hundreds of different tones. After letting the first layer dry completely before applying the second coat, I painted the jar lantern with a combination of teal and pastel yellow on day two. As a result of each layer sitting on top of the previous one without blending into the mud, the gradients were clear and produced a pleasant glow when a tea light flickered within. This demonstrates that the pigmentation is robust enough to stand on its own rather than only serving as accents, since even the lighter colors, which are often weaker in other markers, covered the black glass with confidence.

Sentence: They are super cool and fun to use.
Content:
I really love my new Acrylic Paint Markers! They are super cool and fun to use. The colors are so bright and cover perfectly, even on dark rocks or black paper. I painted a rock with a rainbow design, and it only took one coat because the markers are opaque. I used the markers on wood, glass, and fabric, and the paint stuck well and didn’t fade. After everything dried, the pictures looked like real artwork. My friends were impressed. I think these paint pens are awesome for any art project.

Sentence: It wasn't possible to get a solid color on shiny paper like the color chart that came with the markers.

Sentence: This set comes in a really nice canvas-style case with a sturdy zipper and a fold-out section that holds all 72 colors neatly.
Content:
This set comes in a really nice canvas-style case with a sturdy zipper and a fold-out section that holds all 72 colors neatly. The organization makes it easy to see and grab whichever color you want.

A color chart was included but the slick, shiny surface of the chart doesn’t work well with these markers. On regular paper, though, they work great! The colors are bright, saturated, and really pop.

The set includes both brush tips and hard fine tips. You can get fine, delicate lines with the brush tip (great if you have a steady hand for small details) or bolder lines with the fine tip. Honestly, the difference between a light touch vs. heavy hand feels about the same across both tips, but they’re versatile enough to work for most projects.

The flow is smooth and consistent, with no skipping, and the array of colors is wonderful — there’s something for every idea. I bought this set mainly for making cards and after testing them I can’t wait to use them for the next birthday card. Overall, I’m really happy with this set!

Content:
I ordered these to use in adult coloring books and for colorizing stamped images as well as various other art applications. I LOVE them.

I would definitely pick up another one if I ever get to the point of using up most of the colors. I think this set is well worth the spend.

Sentence: I had no clue, but the vivid colors and multimedia options made this set irresistible.
Content:
Beautiful palette of rich, gorgeous paint markers. What’s a paint marker? I had no clue, but the vivid colors and multimedia options made this set irresistible. They feel like markers but deliver the impact of paint: not messy, just richer and more saturated, with precise application.
The double-tip pens give you options, fine or bold, and every color I tried was vibrant and beautiful. Yes, they work on glass! Perfect for seasonal window art, mirror messages, mason jar labels, handmade gifts, greeting cards, and crafts. The glass application can be removed with a stiff brush, fingernail, or dish soap.
I tested them on foil (hello, freezer meals!), fabric (school/camp labeling), and even Halloween pumpkins. Smooth cotton worked great; textured fabric was less precise but still held up through the washer and dryer.
On smooth surfaces, you can wipe away while still moist, no mess. Once dry, it can be scraped off or removed with solvent. Porous surfaces like fabric are more permanent, so use with care. Kids can absolutely use this if supervised and wearing art clothes or coverups.

Sentence: To summarize, I think it is a decent value for mixed-media use, especially for use with kids.
Content:
Since I enjoy all kinds of crafts and have crafty kids, I was excited to try this set of acrylic markers from Artecho. To summarize, I think it is a decent value for mixed-media use, especially for use with kids. However, a lack of quality control and many similar colors may not satisfy an adult artist.

Pros: I have used many types of non-toxic and paint markers in the past on a variety of mediums, and was thrilled to receive 72 colors in this set. The brush heads are smooth and a delight to work with. The fine tips most resemble traditional press-down paint marker tips, though you don't have to press these down to work - a real improvement! The rainbow of colors is very attractive in the protective, easy-to-transport case. All markers can be easily accessed when the case is open.

Now for the drawbacks. Some of the paints look best on shiny surfaces, but tend to rub off when touched, even after drying. Once fully dried, the acrylic has the best staying-power on matte surfaces without using a fixative. Some of the colors are really beautiful and smooth ("carmine", "sapphire"). Others are weakly pigmented or look muddy ("watermelon", "emerald"). The weak pigments don’t cover darker surfaces or lines, so beware if you’re trying to layer. I was super disappointed at the noticeable difference between the color of the brush and fine tip on many of the markers. See the picture of the color chart: the upper half of each box is the brush side, and the lower half of the box is the fine tip. In most cases, the brush color was quite a bit more pigmented and vibrant than the fine tip color. This difference means I cannot switch between tip types and expect my work to look consistent.

The numbering system and color names seem illogical, and the markers are not organized in the case according to either the numbering or the color chart. Many of the names inadequately reflect the actual color; for example, "brown" is a light pink, and "indigo" is a greenish gray. "Blackberry" and "crimson" are both pale pink. In fact, 18 of the markers are pink tones, including "beige", "camel", and "earth red", and similar in appearance. As the paints are not true to the color of their lids, it is hard to find particular shades unless you rearrange them and use a color chart. However, the included chart lists 120 colors, and there are only 72 in this set, leaving many blank boxes. The color chart is also printed on shiny paper, so the colors tend to smear.

Overall, I think the value of this introductory set is fine at its current price point (24 u.s.d. at the time of review). The markers will be good for painting on stones, wood, and other mixed media crafts with kids (especially kids who like pink), and I think they'll hold up through multiple projects. However, if you're a serious artist or looking to add to your existing stock of acrylic markers, I don't recommend this set from Artecho.

Sentence: What I liked most is that the ink always comes out smooth—no random blobs or dried-up tips, which is usually what annoys me with other markers.
Content:
I grabbed these paint markers for some rainy day projects with my nephews, and they ended up being a hit for everyone. The colors are super bold and actually look good even on stuff like rocks or old jars we found around the house. What I liked most is that the ink always comes out smooth—no random blobs or dried-up tips, which is usually what annoys me with other markers.

We tried them on a bunch of surfaces like fabric, wood, and even some glass. They held up really well after drying, even when my nephew accidentally got water on his painted rock. The dual tips are handy, too; the brush side makes it easy to color big spaces or add details without switching pens every two seconds

Sentence: Function wise, the colors really pop on smooth surfaces like stones and our glass cups, and they go on nice and even without streaks or patchy spots.
Content:
We tried this set of acrylic paint markers for some DIY projects at home, especially rock painting. My 8YO daughter had a blast using them, she polished some stones she picked up and drew little patterns and even fully colored a few of them. Function wise, the colors really pop on smooth surfaces like stones and our glass cups, and they go on nice and even without streaks or patchy spots. Once dry, the paint doesn’t smudge and looks quite professional for a kids’ project. We kept a few of the painted stones as little decorations around the house, they are super cute.

We did run into a small issue when using these markers on regular paper. The ink bleeds through standard A4 sheets pretty easily. My daughter used them on her bed (oops), and the ink soaked through and left some spots on the sheet underneath, which we’re still trying to clean. So just a heads-up: definitely use a backing board or thick pad underneath if you're working on anything thin.

Sentence: I was able to swatch out all the colors in my swatch book and on the included white and black swatch papers.
Content:
This is a very nice set of acrylic markers. There are 36 markers with a brush tip that by the pressure you use when using them you will get thin to fat lines. You can also make dots with the tips of the pens. I was able to swatch out all the colors in my swatch book and on the included white and black swatch papers. You also get some other items to color which I haven't done yet. I only had trouble with one pen, B88, where I could not get the cap off even with gripping it with a silicon gripper. I finally had to ask my husband to see if he could remove the cap and with some big effort, he was able to. When I looked closely at the pen once the cap was off, it was evident that there had been a ink leak that had dried and basically glued the cap on.

I do like the assortment of colors. I like how they swatched in my book and the white swatch card that came with the pens. The black swatch card the colors seemed to be streaky with the coverage not being very good. I do like the pen holder. It is easy to open each tray and to put them back. The colors come out opaque. You get a silver and a gold pen as well as black and white.

I do appreciate the opportunity to try out these pens. Thank you

Sentence: This marker set includes a lot of markers, with all the colors seeming to be different and fairly closely matched to the cap color.
Content:
This marker set includes a lot of markers, with all the colors seeming to be different and fairly closely matched to the cap color.  These only have one tip, which is a fairly stiff brush tip.  It was not flexible enough to use the tip on small areas - seemed to only color at one width.

I only tested these on paper, and while they were ok for kids coloring, might work better on other surfaces, like rocks, plastic, or glass.  Darker colors seemed to work better for drawing over an existing color, while lighter colors were not as opaque.  They weren’t too “wet”, so they didn’t make the paper wet, and they do not bleed through the page, so could be used on dual sided pages.

While they look nice coming in a case, the case does not seem too practical to me at all … it is difficult to line the trays up and get them hooked together correctly … a single plastic box will probably work better.

Sentence: I have been using old-school, strong-smelling, quick-to-dry-out paint pens for many years, but when I saw these WUO acrylic paint markers that didn’t require pressing and holding, I had to try them.
Content:
I have been using old-school, strong-smelling, quick-to-dry-out paint pens for many years, but when I saw these WUO acrylic paint markers that didn’t require pressing and holding, I had to try them. What I wasn’t expecting was how much better they would be.

* Color Range & Appearance: I went with the 60-color set, and I’m glad I did. The colors cover a nice spectrum, including a few pale shades that don’t look obvious from the pen exteriors. For example, the pens made me think there was no pale green, but once tested, there were actually a couple of lighter greens. I’d still love to see extra black, white, gold, and silver included, since those get used up quickly.

* Application & Coverage: The paint goes on somewhat thin (not thick and globby), which turns out to be a strength. It allows layering and blending instead of clumping or streaking. On paper, the coverage is smooth and much nicer than regular markers. On ceramics, you’ll likely need more than one coat like I did. They also work over other acrylic paints (a little tougher on ones that dry glossy, I found), but I find they perform best directly on unfinished ceramic surfaces.

* Packaging & Storage: The set comes in stackable plastic trays that look neat and high-end. Each tray snaps securely into the one below it: tilt the back down first, then lower the front, and finally lock it with the white toggle on the front. I really like this design for keeping them organized.

* Extras: There are tester cards so you can preview how each color looks on black and white paper, plus some small project ideas. One even involves painting onto a sponge, adding water, and watching it puff up, which was fun.

* Odor & Safety: Unlike traditional paint pens, these have no odor at all, which surprised me. That makes them much more pleasant to use and safe for children, though you’d still want to be careful about clothing and surfaces.

* Use Case: I definitely plan to use these for craft projects, but I'm thinking that I'll also use them for detail work on larger acrylic canvas paintings that I do. They shake easily to refresh the paint flow when needed, and I haven’t had issues with clogging. Just avoid pressing too hard on the tips since that could damage them.

* Wishlist for Improvement:
⦁ Pen exterior colors don’t always match the actual paint shade.
⦁ Include more duplicate “workhorse” colors (black, white, gold, silver).
⦁ Offer a fine liner option (about half the tip width) for super-detailed work.

* Value for the Cost: At 39.99 at the time I'm writing this, that's not cheap for a set of craft pens. But, this is a really large set and if  you were to buy each pen individually you would pay much more. Plus you're getting craft projects to go with it. So, all in all, I think this is an exceptional value for the cost...which I hope doesn't change.

* Bottom Line: These paint pens exceeded my expectations. The colors are vibrant, the pens layer and blend well, they store easily, and best of all, they’re odor-free. They make me want to reach for them instead of my old paint pens. Super highly recommended. Go for the kit of 60 if you regularly do crafts and/or use acrylic paints.

Overall, this set is smooth, versatile, and thoughtfully packaged. A fun and practical choice for artists and crafters alike!

Sentence: Moreover, the color swatch on the bottom of the box, is not covered by anything, so all the swatches (this not being real acrylic which is plastic, but some cheap craft gouache) have mostly scraped off within a week from just gently moving the box around.Some of these are actually very decently pigmented, more than other brands, which was a pleasant shock.
Content: This TECADA 168 Colors Acrylic Paint Brush Markers is a weird mix of really good and really not good. I am a professional artist, and I own thousands of acrylic markers, to be able to compare to. The first red flag I see is that the name is Tecada, but the item I received is called Flysea markers. They use the exact same box as a ton of other Chinese paint markers, and the same random extremely unhelpful number system. I was quite worried this would just be a duplicate of other sets I have.The next red flag is that these markers are brand new, but already the numbers - the literal only way to distinguish each marker from each other - are half wiped off. That has already rendered some of them virtually impossible to use.I was fortunate to receive all the markers in the box, and for the most part they are all distinct colors. The box is not good though - competing brands include a zip case organizer with elastic strap loops, and that is far more worth one's money, to be able to keep these in the color order you need them - but good luck taking the time to re-sort all 168 by color order. Moreover, the color swatch on the bottom of the box, is not covered by anything, so all the swatches (this not being real acrylic which is plastic, but some cheap craft gouache) have mostly scraped off within a week from just gently moving the box around.Some of these are actually very decently pigmented, more than other brands, which was a pleasant shock. Most have low opacity though, and you'll be using a lot of layers for a long time spent, if you actually want to color over anything completely. This is more of a layering marker. I was also pleased that generally speaking, these are not an exact match to my other sets - even those with essentially the same box and unmarked markers. They do NOT say Guangna, which is great, because nearly all of this type when you buy them under whatever random name, what you receive is a marker that says GuangNa on the side, and those are both very translucent, and also often very repetitive. These are no-name.Another major good point was that these are as waterproof as POSCA or other similar markers... which is to say, mostly. They, like those, can have a slight bleed with certain colors, or other paints.The best part of this set is that the color swatches are arranged by color, even though the numbers make no sense. That is the one thing that makes this the most usable.The color range is decent, with a few actual dark colors, and a few more realistic greens than most have. This set does not have any actual dark brown - only very chalky browns - and it does not have enough reds. There is not 1 single actual orange in the whole set. Don't buy this looking for orange.Overall, this is a hit and miss set, that for what it offers seems way overpriced to me. When ordered, it was a whopping $77. But I personally would not pay more than maybe $45, given the tons of competing markers on the market. But this really all depends on what you are expecting to do with this. If you need it to be opaque, look elsewhere. If you want layering, and a new range of colors, with some actual darks, this may be a good addition to your collection. I really liked some of the unusual colors provided, that are unlike those in other sets - some more complex grays, a deep red and green, a decent yellow range.For me personally, I would never recommend buying this to anyone, until they fix the markers so the number labeling actually STAYS on the marker. They, and all the time you spent coloring in the swatches - are absolutely useless if you cannot identify any of the markers. If not, that would transform this to a set only useful for 6 year olds. And who is going to spend $77 on a set of markers for 6 year olds? Not me. That price is for people who are actually serious about their coloring, and who are at the least serious crafters, if not semi-pro artists.This set is very low quality, mixed with some random high quality elements, and some well-pigmented colors.

Sentence: They go on super smooth and dry quickly, which is great because I hate waiting around for paint to set.The tips are soft and flexible, kind of like a brush, so they’re easy to control whether I’m coloring in larger areas or doing smaller details.
Content: As someone who loves crafting but isn’t exactly a pro artist, I have to say—I love these paint pens. The Tecada 168 set is a total game-changer for me.First of all, the color range is insane. There are so many shades to play with—brights, pastels, metallics—you name it. I’ve used them on everything from rocks and wood to canvas and even glass jars. They go on super smooth and dry quickly, which is great because I hate waiting around for paint to set.The tips are soft and flexible, kind of like a brush, so they’re easy to control whether I’m coloring in larger areas or doing smaller details. And the ink is really pigmented—most colors only need one layer, which I appreciate.One thing I’ll mention: a few pens needed a good shake and pump to get going, especially the lighter colors. But once they’re flowing, they work beautifully. I just make sure to store them horizontally and cap them tightly when I’m done.Overall, I’m really impressed. These pens are fun, vibrant, and super easy to use. Whether you’re doing DIY projects, journaling, or just messing around with art, I totally recommend them!

Sentence: The color of the paint was true and I was very impressed that none of the colors I tried had any issues with writing, no skipping and didn't have to press the top get the ink to come out which made it easy and efficient to use.
Content: I do crafts/painting as a side business so I was ready not to like these. I doubt a professional would consider these quality but for my purposes and especially for kids, I was impressed.The markers themselves are good, I did notice some leaking inside the marker, but not outside (might be normal for these?). I did a test sheet and it dried pretty quickly. The color of the paint was true and I was very impressed that none of the colors I tried had any issues with writing, no skipping and didn't have to press the top get the ink to come out which made it easy and efficient to use. I also used them on drop cloth in the pic and it worked pretty well, I was very pleased.The case it comes in is just okay, this is the reason for only 4 stars. I wish either the top where you can color in a box for a color sample OR the markers in the case were organized. I tried for about 5 mins to find a matching number and gave up. If you have 20, not a huge deal but 70+ it is. So this is fixable for yourself once you get it and organize it but just know that the functionality of the case may take you some time.I think overall this is good value for the money and it functions as it should so if the case doesn't bother you, I recommend it.

Sentence: Given how easily the paint can be scraped, I'm skeptical about the longevity on plastic or glass.The set does come with a few replacement nibs, should you need them.
Content: This is a very nice set of 168 acrylic paint pens, offering a nice color palette.  The paint flows very smoothly, and has good coverage. The tips are suitable for a wide variety of painting styles, including calligraphy. Adherence to paper and canvas is quite good, but the dried paint can easily be scraped off of coated surfaces, so the recommendation by the manufacturer to utilize a clear top coat is a wise one. Given how easily the paint can be scraped, I'm skeptical about the longevity on plastic or glass.The set does come with a few replacement nibs, should you need them.  I'll note that one of the pens was dried out, with both the nib and the internal wick clogged with dried acrylic paint, and it could not be salvaged. It's possible that the cap wasn't fully sealed during shipment.At the price per pen, I wouldn't expect professional quality, so I'm satisfied.

Sentence: I love the brush tips, and they make brush lettering super easy, getting really great thick and thin strokes.
Content: This 168 color set of acrylic paint markers is a mixed bag. There were a couple that were pretty dry, but most of them work perfectly and lay down opaque colors nicely. I love the brush tips, and they make brush lettering super easy, getting really great thick and thin strokes. I like that they can be used on paper, wood, fabric, canvas, glass, stone, etc. I mostly use them on paper and canvas. The ink flows smoothly and dries quickly to a vibrant, opaque finish that holds up pretty well on different surfaces. My biggest issue with this set is the storage container. It is hard to get the markers out when a row is completely full. There is no rhyme or reason to how the markers are organized. Not by color and not by number. The swatch card is on top of the box and it’s a slick paper. The paint can be scratched off of it easily. Plus, again, the numbers are not organized… I had to search for each and every color number I wanted to swatch. 168 times. Also some of the numbers on the caps aren't legible. It was very frustrating. They do come with a few extra tips.

Sentence: Unfortunately, metallic gel pens clogs easily and also scratches the paper because I need to apply more pressure to get the ink to flow.
Content:
I craft handmade art greetings cards for my friends rather than buy commercial ones. There have been times that I need metallic ink to sign or title my card art. Unfortunately, metallic gel pens clogs easily and also scratches the paper because I need to apply more pressure to get the ink to flow. Marker inks are iffy about bleeding through paper card stock.

Prudiut's 12 Pack Metallic Markers handles card stock art paper well. It dries so fast that there is no bleed through using the brush tip for coloring. The paint remains on the top of the paper. Because the marker paint dries really fast, by the time I grab and open another pen color, the previous paint is dry enough to add dots and details. No smudges on my hands or on the art because the paint dries so quickly.

The pens feels more like painting than drawing. The metallic paint markers flow smoothly like brushed on paint. I am also going to use the metallic markers to highlight and sign my acrylic paintings on canvas. I think the metallic markers would be excellent on adding make-up effects on my handmade ceramic dolls.

The only mess I had with the markers is when taking the caps off. The caps are so stuck on to the pens, that it takes a bit of force to pull off which results in me accidentally getting paint on the fingers that are pulling the cap off. The paint does not rub off when it dries on my skin but it does wash off easy with hand soap and water.

Overall, I am very pleased with the performance and color of Prudiut's 12 Pack Metallic Markers.

Sentence: The ink/paint flows smoothly from both the fine and brush tips on all tested surfaces and there was no bleed through on either type of paper even with two coats.
Content: This 12 pack of dual tip metallic markers are very pretty with a good variety of shades to choose from. They are not as vibrant as the images show; I have tested them on wood, rocks, watercolor paper and black drawing. The ink/paint flows smoothly from both the fine and brush tips on all tested surfaces and there was no bleed through on either type of paper even with two coats. One coat was enough for my wooden coasters and rock projects; however, I used two coats on some spots on the coasters for a deeper color. Some of the colors definitely look more metallic than others and the colors on the back of the box do not match the actual markers making it was difficult to distinguish some of them; names of colors on the pens would have been more helpful. I colored over the chart on the back with each marker so that I could see the difference; red and rose red are confusing me still. I love the colors regardless and these are a nice addition to my growing collection of paint pens. I would absolutely recommend these and $8.99 is a great price for this 12 pack though I’d personally have chosen the 24 pack if it had been offered to me and would be more likely to purchase that for its $14.99 price tag.

Sentence: They are easy to use (no priming, no shaking, just uncap and get to creating!), and they write beautifully.
Content:
This set of acrylic markers has exceeded my expectations. They are easy to use (no priming, no shaking, just uncap and get to creating!), and they write beautifully. They would be awesome for general painting applications on pretty much any surface but would also function very nicely for hand lettering.
They dry quickly - but not instantly, so be careful not to smudge them. Wait a few seconds, though and after that they stay put.
The color range of these markers is really interesting. They're all vibrant and well-pigmented, and there is a range of both standard bright shades, a few fluorescents, and even a really nice range of Morandi-style muted tones that are just gorgeous. There are also a gold and silver metallic that shine so nicely!
They generally provide good coverage, though some of the paler shades are a lot more translucent than I'd like (but it seems that's a problem across almost every brand, save a few. I put down some black and then tried the white over the top and it was not opaque at all. Aside from maybe 4 or 5 of the palest shades though, most of these markers will likely work well on black paper and other darker surfaces.
The brush tips are very nice. They're not all exactly consistent in firmness or in juiciness, but none of them were dry and all of them are quite functional (just some are juicier than others).
I'm concerned a bit about how long these will last since each pen contains two different colors, so the capacity for each color may be less than you would find in a single-color pen, but time will tell!
I look forward to trying their single-color acrylic markers soon, too. These rival most of the other brands that I own, and I can't say enough good things about not having to prime and shake before use.

Sentence: The downside is that if you aren't careful (and honestly, even if you are), the tips of the brushes can break down farely quickly, which makes more detailed work very hard.
Content:
I have the smaller 36 pack of dual Grabie markers, so when I saw they had come out with a larger pack, I grabbed them up.:)

They are the same size and quality as the smaller pack, although the coloring on the marker packaging is different (relief). They also seem to have gone through a color name and number change for some of the colors that were included in the 36; you'll find most of the 36 pack here (with some that look slightly different). This pack covers a wide variety of colors, and there weren't really any (for this coloring anyways) that I was wishing were included.

I absolutely love that these don't have to be primed, and they have brush tips instead of hard nibs. The downside is that if you aren't careful (and honestly, even if you are), the tips of the brushes can break down farely quickly, which makes more detailed work very hard. They can also get bits of dried paint on them, so be prepared to pick the little bits off.
As of writing this, I don't think Grabie offers replacement tips, but I believe they are pretty similar to another brands brush tips, that you can buy replacements for, fairly cheap.

The really lovely thing about these is that they don't bleed through (like some acrylics have separation liquid that leaks through). You can easily color a double sided page, and have zero issues come through the back (given your paper quality, super thin types might show through, I'm unsure).

There's mutliple ways to use these; on rocks, glass paper, vinyl, plastic, etc (given you have a sealant) and I'm still finding extra uses for them, like adding details to coloring pages, or fixing some art when I've gone outside the lines with the medium I'm using, or even to bring back the original color on clay that's darkened too much.

They're very opaque, so you do need to be careful when coloring in pages; you'll want to have a fineliner ready to go over lines if you color over, as these will either soften the lines, or completely wipe them out. You need to be slow while coloring portions in, because if you are fast, you'll get streaks or blotches in the paint (like some areas of my coloring page; book is A Million Kittens). Do make sure to shake them prior to using to blend them.

My main gripe is that they really downgraded on the carry case packaging. I love the 36 pack case; it's softer plastic and textured, with no sharp edges, and it's easy to pull the markers out (and put them back).
With this larger pack, the packaging is a thicker, cheaper plastic that I can't get the markers out, or put them away, without scraping my hands up from the sharp opening. It can be frustrating. I really wish they'd stayed with the same packaging.

I do really like these and they've gone into my travel art bag. My original pack has yet to run out of ink, so they seem like they last a good bit. I'll have to report back if/when they do.

Sentence: I don't know why they don't make a color card and take a picture of it, but this discrepancy has been very normal with already primed paint markers.These acrylic paint markers come primed.
Content: I love paint markers. I'm not sure there's an entirely logical process here... I don't use them anywhere near as much as I should given how many I've gotten, but I identified as an artist in my youth, and having fun art supplies readily available is a lot like breathing fresh air for me.I have ordered at least a half dozen paint marker packs through Vine, including several other sets from GuangNa. Generally, they earn 4 stars from me. I have been very frustrated by their lack of true green shades in their other sets. This set covers it. Wow, does it cover it.Some things you should know if you get this: Numbers are in the 600s, 700s, and 800s. For numbers that could be easily confused, they put a small dot in the upper left to indicate the top of the number. I show this in my video.For filling in your own color card, the row closest to it was almost entirely the left side, and you gradually move right as you go through each row. There are exceptions, but this helped me save time searching for the correct square once I realized.You may note the colors are not exact matches of the printed colors in many cases. I don't know why they don't make a color card and take a picture of it, but this discrepancy has been very normal with already primed paint markers.These acrylic paint markers come primed. You do not need to shake/press to prepare them for use, and these are much easier to control than the kinds that require priming. However, these are also more matte in appearance when dried and relatively easy to scratch. Plan to use a sealant or similar to protect your paintings done with these markers. It's a question of trade-offs. I prefer the ease of use these provide even knowing more work is necessary to protect my creations. You may not.Regardless, I'm thrilled with the color selection of these markers. I can't wait to do more with them!

Sentence: This is a nice set of fine tip acrylic markers with a good range of colors.
Content: This is a nice set of fine tip acrylic markers with a good range of colors. The pens are a little hard. On a fresh pen you can see the paint slowly saturating the tip and one side usually fills faster. The pens work well once started and lay down consistent, clean lines. The firm tips feel durable but wear down with heavy use. My 10 year old used the black for outlining and the tip widened from 0.7 mm to about 2 mm, though it still works fine. The paint is opaque and dries fast, making it great for layering but not for blending.The set includes a small sketchbook with about 20 thick cardstock pages in white, gray, purple, and black, plus two swatch sheets.I do like paint pens, but I got these mostly for my kids. They were super excited and love them. Overall it feels worth the price and works nicely for arts and crafts.

Sentence: They give a nice fine point for exact application and bright colors for your crafts.
Content: These are acrylic paint pens with a variety of applications.I’ve used these for so many things. I’ve used them to label notebooks, on page tabs where I wanted a little color, on the office coffee Keurig, on plastic cups, on rocks, and on regular paper and coloring books.They dry relatively fast, however, they are not for layering. You get an opaque finish with one coat on both non/porous and porous surfaces, but you really can’t go over it again with the same color or another color. It will pull the original layer off on non-porous and it will soak right through on porous.I still like them. They give a nice fine point for exact application and bright colors for your crafts.

I’ve used them on a variety of surfaces — wood, rocks, glass, metal, plastic, canvas, and even fabric — and the coverage and color vibrancy are consistently excellent.  Each pen has a smooth, fine point tip that allows for precise detailing and clean lines, which makes them perfect for outlining, lettering, or adding intricate designs. The flow of paint is steady and even — no blotching or skipping — and the colors are rich, opaque, and quick-drying.  The 18 pack color selection. is beautiful, with a good balance of bright tones and neutral shades. All of the colors layer nicely when dry. I also appreciate that they don’t have a strong chemical smell like some other paint pens.  The acrylic ink quality is top-notch as it’s permanent once dry, waterproof, and resistant to fading or scratching. I’ve made several painted rocks and decorated mugs, and the designs have held up perfectly over time. The pens are also easy to activate: just shake, press the tip a few times, and the ink starts flowing smoothly.  I also love that the set comes well-packaged, with each pen clearly labeled and capped tightly to prevent drying out. The pens are comfortable to hold, lightweight, and the fine tips haven’t frayed or clogged even after multiple uses.  Cleanup is minimal — the paint dries fast, and there’s no smudging or bleeding. For crafts, journaling, DIY gifts, or detailed artwork, these pens are incredibly versatile and reliable.  Overall, the Grabie Acrylic Paint Pens deliver professional-level results at a great price. They’re vibrant, precise, long-lasting, and fun to use on almost any surface. Highly recommend for anyone who loves art, crafting, or adding a creative touch to everyday items!

Sentence: They're highly pigmented, include rich and intense colors, with a good range for a set of 18.
Content: The markers in this set are fantastic. They're highly pigmented, include rich and intense colors, with a good range for a set of 18. You do need to prime them prior to using, and make sure to shake them really well before each use. If you do that, you will not be disappointed in their performance.They are quite opaque, even the white. Again, if you don't shake them well enough, you won't get good coverage with them. The white marker rivals the opacity of the white Posca marker. Not completely 100% opaque, but pretty darn close. With a second coat, you get great coverage.The pens are a little spattery if you're not super careful with them. I'm guessing that this is due to the plastic nib. If you're very careful, you can sort of control that, though.I will say that I really dislike the numbering system. The numbers are sometimes impossible to read, and they seem to be backwards, so to read them correctly you'd have to read them by looking inside the cap. On some of the colors you cannot see the numbers at all, so I abandoned the numbers entirely while swatching them.I absolutely love the little sketchbook that came with this set. It has multiple colors of paper and it's nice, heavy paper, very cardstock-like and has the tiniest bit of tooth. The swatch template included is really creative, and I really appreciate that they provide both a black and white swatch page so you can see how each color performs on both dark and light surfaces (and the colors look VERY different on each).The ink dries pretty quickly with a single coat. With multiple coats (like if you need full coverage on dark paper) does take longer.Generally, these markers work great and I will be using them often.These markers would make a great gift for coloring enthusiasts or the artist in your life, whether they're a beginner or  more experienced.Overall, I highly recommend these markers!
